old_fields.text: Targeted check of the absolute-cone and strip examples. Under the standard radial convention, away from the cone vertex the absolute cone on B has the product coordinates B×(0,1]. For any 0<a<1, the strip B×[a,1] is a collar neighborhood of the outer section B×{1}; the coordinate u=(1-r)/(1-a) sends that section to u=0 and gives B×[0,1]. For a positive radius lambda, the same construction on [a lambda,lambda] collars the section B×{lambda} inside the truncated cone T_lambda. This requires lambda>0; the source’s line does not state its range anew, and no assertion about the vertex radius zero is inferred. For a product strip B×[a,b] with a<b, each endpoint section has a collar obtained by a sufficiently short endpoint subinterval. Their union has a collar by choosing two disjoint endpoint subintervals and taking the disjoint union of those product collars. Therefore the three listed boundary choices are valid if the live barred-E-p operator denotes that radial strip and 0<epsilon<1. The operator is not defined on this leaf, so that identification and parameter range remain explicit hypotheses, not purported recovered definitions. The first epsilon/delta reading remains unresolved despite the expected strip formula.

old_fields.text: Targeted check of the opening equivalence: for a continuous map, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B)=closure(f^{-1}(B)) for every B. Continuity supplies closure(f^{-1}(B)) subset f^{-1}(closure B); openness supplies the reverse by testing an open neighborhood U of x against B. Conversely, the reverse inclusion for every B makes f(U) open by taking B=Y minus f(U). No continuity hypothesis is written here. Without it, openness alone does not give equality: the identity bijection from the two-point indiscrete space to the two-point discrete space is open, but for a singleton B the left side is the singleton and the right side is the entire two-point space. This refutes only an unqualified reading of the displayed claim, not the standing continuity hypothesis explicitly visible on the preceding scan004, which the main reader has checked. The source is not corrected.

operations.old_value: Independent re-proof of the closing finite-union statement under the compact-Hausdorff convention, and assuming the uncertain lower J/I denotes the same finite index set as the preceding family. Let Y_i be finitely many pairwise disjoint closed subsets of compact Hausdorff X, and write Y for their union. Each Y_i is clopen in Y. If h:Y×[0,1]→T is a collar with h(y,0)=y and T a neighborhood of Y, then h(Y_i×[0,1]) is a neighborhood of Y_i: its product component is open in T, and intersecting it with an ambient open neighborhood of Y contained in T gives an ambient open neighborhood of Y_i. The restricted h is its collar. Conversely choose pairwise disjoint ambient open neighborhoods U_i of the Y_i, using normality for a finite family. For a collar h_i:Y_i×[0,1]→T_i, the preimage of U_i∩T_i is open and contains the compact zero section Y_i×{0}. A finite subcover by product neighborhoods provides delta_i>0 such that h_i(Y_i×[0,delta_i]) lies in U_i. Each shortened strip is still a neighborhood of Y_i: the smaller relatively open product Y_i×[0,delta_i) intersects an ambient neighborhood contained in T_i. Rescaling each shortened interval and taking the finite disjoint union gives a bijective collar Y×[0,1]→the union of those strips. Continuity follows from the finite clopen decomposition of Y, and its inverse follows either piecewise from the disjoint U_i or from compactness of the domain and Hausdorffness of X. This proves both directions under the stated separation and indexing hypotheses. The source’s “une partie finie” is retained; it can mean a finite collection here and is not changed to H’s proposed famille.

notes.text: English: This handwritten leaf continues a discussion of local inertia groups and their proposed independence from the model X. It defines the stratum D_J^* by I(x)=J, writes the closed intersection as Delta_J, and asserts regularity and codimension d=card J, allowing the empty set. Hypotheses on the divisors are not restated here and their geometric sufficiency was not checked.

The oblique note now reads D_J as a subscheme followed by an inclusion sign before the closed intersection, and then defines its underlined support by I(x)=J. Conditional on I(x) being the incidence-index set, the full intersection has support I(x) containing J, whereas equality excludes extra divisors. The recovered inclusion sign permits a subscheme contained in that intersection with the exact-incidence stratum as support; the earlier possible mismatch is therefore not forced by the text. No regularity or model-independence theorem is proved here.

There is one written (36), upright with the main display. The independent audit corrects the first reading’s mistaken attachment of this number to the oblique margin. It is retained once as the display tag. The thin bottom-left 131 remains a foliation entry; its hand is not attributed to the author.

English: The source has no opening parenthesis before ou in the fourth line, although a closing parenthesis remains after de tels sous-groupes. It is not supplied. The large curve before et me convaincre is the leader from pour x variable. Four separate dots follow I_V in the first line.

English: No diagram or drawing is present. The large overbrace in the main equality is mathematical notation and is transcribed with the formula. Line_count counts 20 main text/display rows plus five oblique marginal rows; separate interlinear additions and the folio are inventoried separately.

Conditional set-theoretic check: with I finite and each D_i closed, the exact-incidence set I(x)=J is the closed intersection of the D_j, j in J, minus the finite union of the other D_i. It is therefore open in that closed intersection and locally closed in X. This supports the compatibility of the newly recovered marginal inclusion sign with the stated support, without proving the page’s regularity claim.

The independent audit leaves the last index in the second display uncertain: the preferred transcription has a bare final D, with D_j retained only as an alternative because the terminal curve is crowded against the parenthesis. It also restores the raised contraction after codim and the uncertainty on on; none of these readings is supplied from the expected formula or grammar.

notes.text: English: This handwritten leaf continues a discussion of local inertia groups and their proposed independence from the model X. It defines the stratum D_J^* by I(x)=J, writes the closed intersection as Delta_J, and asserts regularity and codimension d=card J, allowing the empty set. Hypotheses on the divisors are not restated here and their geometric sufficiency was not checked.

The oblique note now reads D_J as a subscheme followed by an inclusion sign before the closed intersection, and then defines its underlined support by I(x)=J. Conditional on I(x) being the incidence-index set, the full intersection has support I(x) containing J, whereas equality excludes extra divisors. The recovered inclusion sign permits a subscheme contained in that intersection with the exact-incidence stratum as support; the earlier possible mismatch is therefore not forced by the text. No regularity or model-independence theorem is proved here.

There is one written (36), upright with the main display. The independent audit corrects the first reading’s mistaken attachment of this number to the oblique margin. It is retained once as the display tag. The thin bottom-left 131 remains a foliation entry; its hand is not attributed to the author.

English: The source has no opening parenthesis before ou in the fourth line, although a closing parenthesis remains after de tels sous-groupes. It is not supplied. The large curve before et me convaincre is the leader from pour x variable. Four separate dots follow I_V in the first line.

English: No diagram or drawing is present. The large overbrace in the main equality is mathematical notation and is transcribed with the formula. Line_count counts 20 main text/display rows plus five oblique marginal rows; separate interlinear additions and the folio are inventoried separately.

Conditional set-theoretic check: with I finite and each D_i closed, the exact-incidence set I(x)=J is the closed intersection of the D_j, j in J, minus the finite union of the other D_i. It is therefore open in that closed intersection and locally closed in X. This supports the compatibility of the newly recovered marginal inclusion sign with the stated support, without proving the page’s regularity claim.

The independent audit leaves the last index in the second display uncertain: the preferred transcription has a bare final D, with D_j retained only as an alternative because the terminal curve is crowded against the parenthesis. It also restores the raised contraction after codim and the uncertainty on on; none of these readings is supplied from the expected formula or grammar.

notes.text: English: The page chooses an L-embedding into the algebraic closure and comments on the construction numbered (37). The author describes a fibre heuristically as a product of discs and writes “j’ai eu un peu peur d’y mettre … zéro à g”, followed by a boundary map pi_2(bar D_J) to pi_1(fibre), identified vertically with T^J, and the explicit question/exclamation “(?)!”. These are the author’s doubts, not editorial conclusions. The construction (37) itself is outside this assigned page.

English: A five-object diagram is used to motivate a morphism between homotopy exact sequences. The source identifies pi_2(xi) with zero and concludes that the composite pi_2(D_J) to T^J to pi_{U/K} is zero. It then states conditionally that injectivity of T^J to pi_{U/K} implies the first boundary map is zero. The formal diagram implication is valid once the displayed commutative morphism of sequences and the stated identifications exist: naturality gives g composed with delta equal to delta-prime composed with a, and a has zero target. If g is injective, delta is zero. No geometric existence of the fibrations, comparison theorem, or asserted injectivity is verified by this formal check.

English: The lower-right group label is not normalized to the mathematically expected E_K: the draft retains K|U because the compressed subscript admits both shapes. The six other stacked identification signs contain a curved upright beside a straight upright; they are encoded consistently as wr plus a vertical stroke, while the two pi_2 identifications and the earlier fibre identification use two straight vertical strokes. None is turned into a horizontal equality.

English: The opening article is le; the added beginning-of-homotopy-sequence phrase attaches before fibré. The first failed reformulation after the injection has both elle and the added devrait cancelled; the later devrait avoir is replaced by a. Relative is replaced by de celle relative, and ligne by colonne. These local revision states are retained individually.

English: There are two genuine commutative diagrams and no separate drawing. The light bottom-left 133 is retained as foliation of unestablished hand. Line_count counts 26 principal text/display/object rows; interlinear revisions, individual arrow-only levels, and foliation are inventoried separately. The blind audit prefers leur before zéro but retains lexical/source-state alternatives. The lower arrowhead doubts and K/U index remain unresolved. The first U_J-to-X_J shaft is now represented with its visible breaks.

English: In the cancelled phrase before commutatif, the apparent p was the long q descender from heuristiquement above. The separate low word is now read une/un under cancellation, even though induit par would be more idiomatic. The diagram audit confirms that the letter above T^J belongs to prose la, and that the relative fundamental-group symbol has the same pi construction as the homotopy-group symbols; no capitalization is inferred from its straight roof.

notes.text: English: The page chooses an L-embedding into the algebraic closure and comments on the construction numbered (37). The author describes a fibre heuristically as a product of discs and writes “j’ai eu un peu peur d’y mettre … zéro à g”, followed by a boundary map pi_2(bar D_J) to pi_1(fibre), identified vertically with T^J, and the explicit question/exclamation “(?)!”. These are the author’s doubts, not editorial conclusions. The construction (37) itself is outside this assigned page.

English: A five-object diagram is used to motivate a morphism between homotopy exact sequences. The source identifies pi_2(xi) with zero and concludes that the composite pi_2(D_J) to T^J to pi_{U/K} is zero. It then states conditionally that injectivity of T^J to pi_{U/K} implies the first boundary map is zero. The formal diagram implication is valid once the displayed commutative morphism of sequences and the stated identifications exist: naturality gives g composed with delta equal to delta-prime composed with a, and a has zero target. If g is injective, delta is zero. No geometric existence of the fibrations, comparison theorem, or asserted injectivity is verified by this formal check.

English: The lower-right group label is not normalized to the mathematically expected E_K: the draft retains K|U because the compressed subscript admits both shapes. The six other stacked identification signs contain a curved upright beside a straight upright; they are encoded consistently as wr plus a vertical stroke, while the two pi_2 identifications and the earlier fibre identification use two straight vertical strokes. None is turned into a horizontal equality.

English: The opening article is le; the added beginning-of-homotopy-sequence phrase attaches before fibré. The first failed reformulation after the injection has both elle and the added devrait cancelled; the later devrait avoir is replaced by a. Relative is replaced by de celle relative, and ligne by colonne. These local revision states are retained individually.

English: There are two genuine commutative diagrams and no separate drawing. The light bottom-left 133 is retained as foliation of unestablished hand. Line_count counts 26 principal text/display/object rows; interlinear revisions, individual arrow-only levels, and foliation are inventoried separately. The blind audit prefers leur before zéro but retains lexical/source-state alternatives. The lower arrowhead doubts and K/U index remain unresolved. The first U_J-to-X_J shaft is now represented with its visible breaks.

English: In the cancelled phrase before commutatif, the apparent p was the long q descender from heuristiquement above. The separate low word is now read une/un under cancellation, even though induit par would be more idiomatic. The diagram audit confirms that the letter above T^J belongs to prose la, and that the relative fundamental-group symbol has the same pi construction as the homotopy-group symbols; no capitalization is inferred from its straight roof.

notes.text: The sheet is a landscape double leaf with handwritten folio 1, a wide left discussion and narrower right continuation. It develops specialization preorders, the associated topology on a preorder, two functors and an adjunction, then asks which preorders a pseudo-partition determines. The upper-right asterisk note asks “quelles conditions supplémentaires ... imposer pour avoir unicité ?”. This is a report of source contents, not verification of its claims.

Several apparent slips are preserved: the NB1 closure equivalence uses a written ≤ where the earlier definition uses subset; the two identity subscripts are written E then O; the Posons insertion appears to use inverse image of I although its left index is J; the summand in the left closure formula is unstarred X_j. These are visual diagnostics only. Parent will append any independently performed mathematical checks.

Source grammar is not regularized. The current text retains cette préordre; the noun/agreement in les réunions ... est fermé is now explicitly doubtful, and singular partition is preferred with partitions as an alternative. The initial capital A before quelles has no written accent. The identity-map explanation still has no closing parenthesis after NB2. No missing word or punctuation has been supplied.

Whole image and both supplied native halves were inspected once; required places P01–P52 were inspected once each. P53 completes only the clipped extreme-right punctuation of P35. P54 inspects previously uncropped specialization underlining. P55 was a clipped context fragment; P56 completes only its missing NB. 2 heading. No OCR, outside research or TeX compilation was used. line_count counts nonempty logical draft lines, including display and diagram rows.

The short horizontal stroke below the adjunction explanation is rendered as a paragraph separator. Its source position starts far left of I→X and lies below the sentence baseline, so it is not assigned as a certain underline.

Targeted check from the definitions on this sheet: x ≤ y iff closure{x} ⊆ closure{y} makes every open upward closed. In the associated preorder topology, closure{x}=I_{≤x}, so its specialization preorder recovers the original one. A map I→X is continuous iff it is monotone: continuity preserves specialization; conversely the inverse image of each X-open is upward closed and therefore open in I. This establishes the stated Hom correspondence under those definitions.

The category labels in the source make Ord∘Esp an endofunctor of O and Esp∘Ord an endofunctor of E. The visually confirmed right-hand identity subscripts are nevertheless E then O. Both are preserved literally; exchanging them is only a typing diagnostic, not an emendation.

Targeted check: closure{i} intersected with the smallest open containing i is the preorder-equivalence class of i. Its equality to {i} for every i is equivalent to antisymmetry. This explains the two opposite decorations in the source; it does not change any written mark.

Targeted check of the local-finiteness claim: if φ has locally finite image, then on a neighborhood of each point only finitely many fibers occur. Restrictions of saturated sets to that neighborhood therefore have only finitely many possible forms. An arbitrary union of saturated closed sets restricts to a finite union of closed restrictions, so is closed locally, hence globally. Thus arbitrary unions of quotient-closed sets are quotient-closed. The source singular agreement and its use of ordre versus préordre remain untouched.

Blind-audit findings: distinguish the unaccented baseline ordonne and left definition label def from separately accented occurrences. The terminal NB1 mark is a dash. The finite-case explanation has a closing parenthesis but no secure opening one. Final finie in the explanation of local finiteness is written with a small e. New uncertainties that preserve the preferred C reading are recorded as doubts, not new primary corrections.

Audit scope limitation: neutral box B18 contains the already-transcribed I→X but misses the paragraph rule. The main reader inspected saved original crop P17, which includes both. The separator is retained on that independent visual evidence; the fixed second reading has not been altered or represented as having read the missing rule.

The lower indexing clause is raised and independently underlined above a separate heavy cancellation. The low group beneath it favors qui filtre, with tels que retained as an alternative. The nearby telle que after disjoints et follows the rising baseline in the wider image; it is not asserted to be a separate insertion.

notes.text: The sheet is a landscape double leaf with handwritten folio 1, a wide left discussion and narrower right continuation. It develops specialization preorders, the associated topology on a preorder, two functors and an adjunction, then asks which preorders a pseudo-partition determines. The upper-right asterisk note asks “quelles conditions supplémentaires ... imposer pour avoir unicité ?”. This is a report of source contents, not verification of its claims.

Several apparent slips are preserved: the NB1 closure equivalence uses a written ≤ where the earlier definition uses subset; the two identity subscripts are written E then O; the Posons insertion appears to use inverse image of I although its left index is J; the summand in the left closure formula is unstarred X_j. These are visual diagnostics only. Parent will append any independently performed mathematical checks.

Source grammar is not regularized. The current text retains cette préordre; the noun/agreement in les réunions ... est fermé is now explicitly doubtful, and singular partition is preferred with partitions as an alternative. The initial capital A before quelles has no written accent. The identity-map explanation still has no closing parenthesis after NB2. No missing word or punctuation has been supplied.

Whole image and both supplied native halves were inspected once; required places P01–P52 were inspected once each. P53 completes only the clipped extreme-right punctuation of P35. P54 inspects previously uncropped specialization underlining. P55 was a clipped context fragment; P56 completes only its missing NB. 2 heading. No OCR, outside research or TeX compilation was used. line_count counts nonempty logical draft lines, including display and diagram rows.

The short horizontal stroke below the adjunction explanation is rendered as a paragraph separator. Its source position starts far left of I→X and lies below the sentence baseline, so it is not assigned as a certain underline.

Targeted check from the definitions on this sheet: x ≤ y iff closure{x} ⊆ closure{y} makes every open upward closed. In the associated preorder topology, closure{x}=I_{≤x}, so its specialization preorder recovers the original one. A map I→X is continuous iff it is monotone: continuity preserves specialization; conversely the inverse image of each X-open is upward closed and therefore open in I. This establishes the stated Hom correspondence under those definitions.

The category labels in the source make Ord∘Esp an endofunctor of O and Esp∘Ord an endofunctor of E. The visually confirmed right-hand identity subscripts are nevertheless E then O. Both are preserved literally; exchanging them is only a typing diagnostic, not an emendation.

Targeted check: closure{i} intersected with the smallest open containing i is the preorder-equivalence class of i. Its equality to {i} for every i is equivalent to antisymmetry. This explains the two opposite decorations in the source; it does not change any written mark.

Targeted check of the local-finiteness claim: if φ has locally finite image, then on a neighborhood of each point only finitely many fibers occur. Restrictions of saturated sets to that neighborhood therefore have only finitely many possible forms. An arbitrary union of saturated closed sets restricts to a finite union of closed restrictions, so is closed locally, hence globally. Thus arbitrary unions of quotient-closed sets are quotient-closed. The source singular agreement and its use of ordre versus préordre remain untouched.

Blind-audit findings: distinguish the unaccented baseline ordonne and left definition label def from separately accented occurrences. The terminal NB1 mark is a dash. The finite-case explanation has a closing parenthesis but no secure opening one. Final finie in the explanation of local finiteness is written with a small e. New uncertainties that preserve the preferred C reading are recorded as doubts, not new primary corrections.

Audit scope limitation: neutral box B18 contains the already-transcribed I→X but misses the paragraph rule. The main reader inspected saved original crop P17, which includes both. The separator is retained on that independent visual evidence; the fixed second reading has not been altered or represented as having read the missing rule.

The lower indexing clause is raised and independently underlined above a separate heavy cancellation. The low group beneath it favors qui filtre, with tels que retained as an alternative. The nearby telle que after disjoints et follows the rising baseline in the wider image; it is not asserted to be a separate insertion.

notes.text: This double manuscript leaf, authorial pages 3 and 4), develops conditions on a locally finite indexed pseudo-partition and its map phi to a preordered set: continuity, final/quotient topology, openness, and non-emptiness. It then describes strict stratifications by increasing closed families, intersections, and the condition that X_j be rare in X_i when j<i. These are contents of the source, transcribed without a theorem proof.

The left condition 3 literally reads bar X_j* = union over j≤i of X_j*, followed by pour tt j in I. The same handwritten j is clear in the left subscript and final quantifier, while the bound ends in i. This free/bound-index mismatch is preserved. The source forms were compared with the nearby definition X_i=union over j≤i X_j*; the comparison identifies a local notation discrepancy and does not license emendation.

The left separation criterion ends with the literal les X_i sont loc. fermés, without stars. Earlier the same page assumes the X_i closed, whereas the later right paragraph explicitly refers to X_i* being locally closed. This internal source comparison flags the missing-star possibility for mathematical review, but the unstarred written X_i remains in the transcription. No proof of the asserted equivalence was attempted.

The vertical déf annotation below X_i* gives X_i minus the union over j<i of X_j, with no star on its summand. The later Moyennant sentence explicitly uses X_j* in that union. Both forms are retained; no equivalence is supplied by editorial emendation.

The lower-left discussion is framed by il faut voir comment and concerns a least moderate strict refinement of a partition by locally closed moderate pieces. The author’s question and the revisions after plus petite are preserved, including unresolved state and plurality of the raised strictes. This is not presented as a verified existence theorem.

The landscape sheet has a central pen divider, two slanted left separator strokes and a horizontal left separator. The isolated upper-right group is written at 180 degrees to the main text and is reproduced upright, preserving uncertain J/I and upper symbols. The authorial numbers are 3 and 4); a thinner lower-left 3 has indeterminate attribution. No date is visible. Pale reversed/show-through matter is excluded.

The quotient criterion has an extra closing parenthesis after X_L* ouvert. In the right uniqueness display the first closing mark is brace-like and remains qualified as brace/parenthesis; the next equivalence has separate parentheses. Curved leaders at loc. finie, croissante, stratifiantes and pour l’ordre donné à I are not separate underlines or parentheses. Fermées has an independent underline.

Openness criterion: For a continuous map f, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B) = closure(f^{-1}(B)) for all B. Continuity supplies the inclusion from the right to the left. Openness supplies the reverse: any neighborhood U of x maps to a neighborhood f(U) of f(x), so f(x) in closure B forces U to meet f^{-1}(B). Conversely this reverse inclusion implies every f(U) is open: if a point y in f(U) were in closure(Y\f(U)), an x in U over y would be in closure(f^{-1}(Y\f(U))), contradicting the open neighborhood U. These checks do not change the source j/i mismatch in its numbered formula.

Local closedness diagnostic: The source identifies each cumulative X_i with a closed union of strata. Such an X_i is automatically locally closed, so the written parenthetical criterion using X_i without a star cannot by itself characterize antisymmetry of the quotient preorder. The intended criterion plausibly concerns X_i^*, but the unstarred ink is retained. This is a diagnostic of the written definitions, not an emendation.

The 3 bis note: Under the page's conditions1,2,4 and local finiteness, the equivalence between nonempty X_i and nonempty X_i^* can be checked locally. The lower closed subsets X_j (j<i) are nowhere dense in X_i under condition4; only finitely many are present near any chosen point by local finiteness. A finite union of closed nowhere dense subsets cannot cover a nonempty open piece of X_i. Thus a nonempty X_i has a point outside their union. This validates the conditional argument of the note without changing its labels or uncertain glyphs.

Independent-reading scope check: B13 clipped the opening quantifier, and B33 clipped most of the intersection formula. The main reader inspected wider original crops P10wide and P25wide and retained those readings. The fixed second reading is not altered. The upright marginal diagram was a substantive orientation correction.

notes.text: This double manuscript leaf, authorial pages 3 and 4), develops conditions on a locally finite indexed pseudo-partition and its map phi to a preordered set: continuity, final/quotient topology, openness, and non-emptiness. It then describes strict stratifications by increasing closed families, intersections, and the condition that X_j be rare in X_i when j<i. These are contents of the source, transcribed without a theorem proof.

The left condition 3 literally reads bar X_j* = union over j≤i of X_j*, followed by pour tt j in I. The same handwritten j is clear in the left subscript and final quantifier, while the bound ends in i. This free/bound-index mismatch is preserved. The source forms were compared with the nearby definition X_i=union over j≤i X_j*; the comparison identifies a local notation discrepancy and does not license emendation.

The left separation criterion ends with the literal les X_i sont loc. fermés, without stars. Earlier the same page assumes the X_i closed, whereas the later right paragraph explicitly refers to X_i* being locally closed. This internal source comparison flags the missing-star possibility for mathematical review, but the unstarred written X_i remains in the transcription. No proof of the asserted equivalence was attempted.

The vertical déf annotation below X_i* gives X_i minus the union over j<i of X_j, with no star on its summand. The later Moyennant sentence explicitly uses X_j* in that union. Both forms are retained; no equivalence is supplied by editorial emendation.

The lower-left discussion is framed by il faut voir comment and concerns a least moderate strict refinement of a partition by locally closed moderate pieces. The author’s question and the revisions after plus petite are preserved, including unresolved state and plurality of the raised strictes. This is not presented as a verified existence theorem.

The landscape sheet has a central pen divider, two slanted left separator strokes and a horizontal left separator. The isolated upper-right group is written at 180 degrees to the main text and is reproduced upright, preserving uncertain J/I and upper symbols. The authorial numbers are 3 and 4); a thinner lower-left 3 has indeterminate attribution. No date is visible. Pale reversed/show-through matter is excluded.

The quotient criterion has an extra closing parenthesis after X_L* ouvert. In the right uniqueness display the first closing mark is brace-like and remains qualified as brace/parenthesis; the next equivalence has separate parentheses. Curved leaders at loc. finie, croissante, stratifiantes and pour l’ordre donné à I are not separate underlines or parentheses. Fermées has an independent underline.

Openness criterion: For a continuous map f, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B) = closure(f^{-1}(B)) for all B. Continuity supplies the inclusion from the right to the left. Openness supplies the reverse: any neighborhood U of x maps to a neighborhood f(U) of f(x), so f(x) in closure B forces U to meet f^{-1}(B). Conversely this reverse inclusion implies every f(U) is open: if a point y in f(U) were in closure(Y\f(U)), an x in U over y would be in closure(f^{-1}(Y\f(U))), contradicting the open neighborhood U. These checks do not change the source j/i mismatch in its numbered formula.

Local closedness diagnostic: The source identifies each cumulative X_i with a closed union of strata. Such an X_i is automatically locally closed, so the written parenthetical criterion using X_i without a star cannot by itself characterize antisymmetry of the quotient preorder. The intended criterion plausibly concerns X_i^*, but the unstarred ink is retained. This is a diagnostic of the written definitions, not an emendation.

The 3 bis note: Under the page's conditions1,2,4 and local finiteness, the equivalence between nonempty X_i and nonempty X_i^* can be checked locally. The lower closed subsets X_j (j<i) are nowhere dense in X_i under condition4; only finitely many are present near any chosen point by local finiteness. A finite union of closed nowhere dense subsets cannot cover a nonempty open piece of X_i. Thus a nonempty X_i has a point outside their union. This validates the conditional argument of the note without changing its labels or uncertain glyphs.

Independent-reading scope check: B13 clipped the opening quantifier, and B33 clipped most of the intersection formula. The main reader inspected wider original crops P10wide and P25wide and retained those readings. The fixed second reading is not altered. The upright marginal diagram was a substantive orientation correction.

notes.text: This landscape handwritten sheet has two columns. The left starts with an openness calculation, continues item 5 on restriction and faithfulness, and ends with local stratifications. The right contains a cancelled attempt followed by a finite minimal-counterexample argument and a heading “3 conditions équiv. :”. The thin lower-left 4 is foliation in another or undetermined hand. There is no typescript. H’s editorial notes and following section heading are not manuscript text.

Targeted check of the opening equivalence: for a continuous map, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B)=closure(f^{-1}(B)) for every B. Continuity supplies closure(f^{-1}(B)) subset f^{-1}(closure B); openness supplies the reverse by testing an open neighborhood U of x against B. Conversely, the reverse inclusion for every B makes f(U) open by taking B=Y minus f(U). No continuity hypothesis is written here. Without it, openness alone does not give equality: the identity bijection from the two-point indiscrete space to the two-point discrete space is open, but for a singleton B the left side is the singleton and the right side is the entire two-point space. This refutes only an unqualified reading of the displayed claim, not the standing continuity hypothesis explicitly visible on the preceding scan004, which the main reader has checked. The source is not corrected.

The final underbrace literally reads B subset X minus V although V=varphi(U) is a subset of Y. The crossed diagonals of X are clear. The argument’s ambient complement would be Y minus V. Independently, the criterion “for all y in V and B subset Y, y in closure B implies V cap B nonempty” is equivalent to V being open: put B=Y minus V to obtain V subset interior V, and use the neighborhood definition of closure for the converse. The written X is retained as a source slip.

Independent order-theoretic check of the right-column deduction, under the down-set meaning of closed used by barred j: assume J is not closed and every closed K with K cap J nonclosed contains J. Choose j in J with down(j) not contained in J. Then K=down(j) has K cap J nonclosed, so J subset down(j), making j the greatest element of J. If j-prime differs from j, down(j-prime) cannot fail to lie in J, since the same argument would force j<=j-prime; hence J_0=J minus {j} is the union of these down(j-prime), and is closed. notes.text: This landscape handwritten sheet has two columns. The left starts with an openness calculation, continues item 5 on restriction and faithfulness, and ends with local stratifications. The right contains a cancelled attempt followed by a finite minimal-counterexample argument and a heading “3 conditions équiv. :”. The thin lower-left 4 is foliation in another or undetermined hand. There is no typescript. H’s editorial notes and following section heading are not manuscript text.

Targeted check of the opening equivalence (refined statement `150_scan005.N02.continuous`): for a continuous map, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B)=closure(f^{-1}(B)) for every B. Continuity supplies closure(f^{-1}(B)) subset f^{-1}(closure B); openness supplies the reverse by testing an open neighborhood U of x against B. Conversely, the reverse inclusion for every B makes f(U) open by taking B=Y minus f(U). No continuity hypothesis is written here. Without it, openness alone does not give equality: the identity bijection from the two-point indiscrete space to the two-point discrete space is open, but for a singleton B the left side is the singleton and the right side is the entire two-point space. This refutes only an unqualified reading of the displayed claim, not the standing continuity hypothesis explicitly visible on the preceding scan004, which the main reader has checked. The source is not corrected.

The final underbrace literally reads B subset X minus V although V=varphi(U) is a subset of Y. The crossed diagonals of X are clear. The argument’s ambient complement would be Y minus V. Independently, the criterion “for all y in V and B subset Y, y in closure B implies V cap B nonempty” is equivalent to V being open: put B=Y minus V to obtain V subset interior V, and use the neighborhood definition of closure for the converse. The written X is retained as a source slip.

The live fork example is checked directly from the displayed formula: let X_a={a}, X_b={b}, and X_c={a,b}, with a<c and b<c. Inclusion among these three nonempty sets gives precisely that poset, so the stated fidelity holds; nevertheless X_c minus the union of its proper predecessor sets is empty. This verifies the local counterexample to deriving nonempty X_c-star from inclusion fidelity. It does not verify unnamed conditions 1°, 2°, 3° bis or 4° from other pages.

The phrase “un ouvert I_U de U” contains a visibly written U. The immediately preceding inserted i in I tels que shows I_U is being defined as a set of indices, so de I would be the expected ambient phrase. The text keeps U and records the mismatch here. The ps prefix in ps-fidèle is live, with a hyphen; retracing is not converted into a separate deleted word.

Independent order-theoretic check of the right-column deduction, under the down-set meaning of closed used by barred j: assume J is not closed and every closed K with K cap J nonclosed contains J. Choose j in J with down(j) not contained in J. Then K=down(j) has K cap J nonclosed, so J subset down(j), making j the greatest element of J. If j-prime differs from j, down(j-prime) cannot fail to lie in J, since the same argument would force j<=j-prime; hence J_0=J minus {j} is the union of these down(j-prime), and is closed. The missing predecessor of j lies outside J, hence outside J_0. A separate finite enumeration checked all 19 labelled partial orders on three elements and all 39 qualifying nonclosed J, with no failures. This checks the local lemma, not the earlier topological premise that produces its hypothesis.

The boundary containment is checked independently: if X_J-star is closed and is the disjoint union of A=X_{J_0}-star and S=X_j-star, then closure(S) subset A union S; subtracting S gives closure(S) minus S subset A. This is exactly the written containment for X_j-bullet. Replacing A by X_{J_0} additionally uses the source’s asserted equality for a closed index set; its definition is not supplied on this leaf.

For the closing a)/b) pair, the complement argument works conditionally if the starred sets form a disjoint covering family: X_{I minus J}-star is the complement of X_J-star, and a subset of I is open exactly when its complement is closed. Thus closedness reflection and openness reflection are equivalent under those definitions. The equivalence with the full condition c), including the unresolved NB abbreviation, is carried as the author’s assertion rather than claimed as verified from this leaf alone. In the earlier greatest-element situation, closure(J)=closure(j), so retaining the written capital-shaped barred J in P28 does not by itself create a mathematical contradiction. The main reader separately checked the preceding leaf’s definitions of conditions1,2,3 bis; see N12 below.

The final line visibly repeats pour, retained against both witnesses’ tout. Its terminal arrow has one shaft, unlike the doubled implication above. The edge word now favors cl, with ch/des alternatives. The compact NB abbreviation favors ops, with sps/ssi alternatives; no expansion is supplied.

All 105 corrected physical rows of the page-only difference TSV were reviewed using splitlines and tabs. The earlier malformed packet was discarded after its out-of-scope rows were noticed; no other page image, witness file or report was opened. Whole image and both supplied native halves were each read once; P01–P32 were each inspected, with P32 limited to the previously clipped c label. The newly identified crossed token between the inner equals and singleton in P18 has no physically supportable candidate. It is represented at its source position by empty-content unsure inside the existing cancellation; the adjacent TeX comment identifies the saved crop. The empty payload means present unreadable ink, not a blank or absent token. This avoids both inventing a symbol and treating an unrecognized mathematical symbol as an illegible-word count.

Main-reader check against scan004: its final 3 bis condition says the cumulative X_i are nonempty. Conditions1 and2 together with that condition do not imply the order-reflecting faithfulness asserted here. On the two-element chain0<1 take the one-point space X and X_0=X_1=X. These closed pieces are increasing and cover X, their intersection equals the union over common predecessors for each pair, and both are nonempty; nevertheless X_1 subset X_0 while1 is not <=0. Thus the stated implication fails under the transcribed definitions. Refined statement `150_scan005.N12.nonempty_strata`: Nonempty strata (condition3) would imply faithfulness by the disjoint-strata argument, but the written3 bis is retained. This check neither changes the source nor claims the author intended an emendation.

Main-reader strengthening of the local boundary check: for closed F and arbitrary A, F union A is closed if and only if closure(A) minus A is contained in F. Indeed closure(F union A)=F union closure(A). With F=X_{J_0} and A=X_j-star this checks the local boundary equivalence, subject to the displayed closedness of F. It does not prove the full concluding three-condition equivalence or remove the source’s finiteness hypotheses.

notes.text: The sheet contains two upper drawings, a flag-indexed contravariant construction, two Sigma formulas with revisions, cofinal marginal diagrams, a V formula and lower diagram, and a slanted marginal parameter equality/inequality. No theorem verification has been performed by this reader. The line_count of 13 counts main prose/formula/object baselines, excluding figure labels, interlinear corrections and marginal material.

The live phrase is "foncteur contravariant par rapport aux drapeaux variables". The cancelled preceding word favors simplicial with covariant retained as an alternative. The marginal word reads cofinaux; no unstated direction or universal property is added.

The Sigma formulas use the strict range k<i or i<k<j. The later V formula visibly uses i<=k<j. This difference is retained, as is its unresolved star/prime exponent; the formulas are not regularized into one convention.

The lower top connector has a left hook and no head. The dashed diagonal branch starts from the right vertical edge and has no labelled destination object. Its annotation and the struck lower-edge annotation remain uncertain. No mathematical map is supplied to fill the missing destination.

The thin top S|5 and underlined lower 6 are transcribed as marginal marks, with hand unassigned. C treated the top mark as author foliation; that attribution is not established from this leaf. H final section heading is editorial, not ink on this page.

The bottom marginal formulas retain asymmetric subscript/prime placement as seen, rather than supplying symmetric indices. The operator reads Inf, not Sigma. The quantities are not defined on this leaf.

Crops P03 and P10 were initially viewed in an upside-down text orientation and read mentally; their saved files were then deterministically rotated 180 degrees without rereading. P14/P15 were displayed individually after a multi-image output omitted them. P06 was reopened only for the newly identified tuple sub-place. P16 completes the clipped lower extent of the rotated margin. The main-text Sigma_(i,j) at its right is not a marginal object. The relation array has only a right vertical cap; no left cap is supplied.

Independent second-reading adjudication: all 17 nonidentical targets were personally inspected by the main reader. Targeted rotation resolved the orientation at B03; root_postXj, root_indexscope and root_labelC address only the outstanding sign, duplication and letter-case questions.

The i<k<j below the second Sigma formula is the insertion at the end of the curved union-index leader. It occurs once. Both supplied witnesses duplicated it as an additional display; inventory E14 was removed as that duplicate, while E13 remains.

Point/dash punctuation is preserved literally in the Sigma flag subscript and tuple. The lower formula intersection index and the large diagram initial-object last index favor n but retain k as an alternative. Neither is made k merely to fit the bound or neighboring labels.

notes.text: The sheet specifies three topological spaces Sigma_0, Sigma_1, Sigma_2 and closed relations Sigma_01, Sigma_12, Sigma_02. It defines Sigma_012 by an intersection of products, then discusses a commutative diagram, injective/bordante maps, Cartesian squares, transversality and fibration conditions. The two marginal notes interpret the data as an order above [0,1,2] and propose a locally trivial three-object diagram over Sigma_0 as the proposed strengthening/replacement of f), with renforcer preferred and remplacer still possible. The first-reader pass records these source contents. The separate root checks in N07–N09 are conditional and set-theoretic; the geometric conditions d)–f) were not verified.

The first inclusion literally repeats Sigma_01 on both sides. H’s main text changes its right side to Sigma_0 times Sigma_1 and acknowledges that emendation in an editorial note. The literal self-inclusion is retained. The two neighbouring product inclusions and the later definition suggest the intended product, but that is an internal-source inference and is not substituted for the ink.

Condition c) literally states Sigma_012=Sigma_02 intersection Sigma_12 dans Sigma_12. The upper diagram arrows have common target Sigma_2. This comparison distinguishes the written dans Sigma_12 from the common space used to form the intersection after the b) identifications; it does not silently replace the written subscript. The root set-theoretic check is recorded separately in N09.

The continued b) target contains an overworked 0-shaped body before 2. Its state remains undecided between live 02 and a cancelled 0 followed by 2. The later et a fortiori map does not decide that ink. Root’s conditional injectivity check in N08 also shows that both target readings are compatible with the injectivity consequences, so mathematical coherence cannot establish a cancellation.

The singular phrase un morphisme bordant in d), singular fibrant in f), mixed delimiter (liss], and comma in the final Sigma_0,12 index are transcribed literally. The unexplained phrase after Cela remains doubtful, and the missing opening parenthesis is not supplied despite a written closing parenthesis.

This is a single foreground handwritten sheet. No authorial page number or written date is visible at its head. A thin lower-left 7 is recorded as foliation with indeterminate attribution. Apparent isolated W/delta forms in H belong to the complete rotated marginal note; faint show-through/paper specks are not transcribed.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of a), conditional on interpreting Sigma_01 as a relation in Sigma_0 times Sigma_1, and similarly the other Sigma_ij, as indicated by the later triple-product formula and diagram. The literal opening self-inclusion does not itself supply that hypothesis. On the disjoint union, adjoin only identities within each level and the indicated relations between increasing levels. Reflexivity then follows from the adjoined identities, and antisymmetry follows from strictly increasing grades for every nonidentity pair. The only possible composition of two nonidentity pairs is 0→1→2; its transitivity requirement is exactly a), the projection of Sigma_012 to (x0,x2) lying in Sigma_02.

Root targeted injectivity check, under the same relational/product interpretation and a) together with the injection hypotheses in b). Given (x1,x2), the injection Sigma_01→Sigma_1 determines x0, so Sigma_012→Sigma_12 is injective. Given (x0,x2), the injection Sigma_12→Sigma_2 determines x1, so Sigma_012→Sigma_02 is injective. Composing the latter map with the assumed injection Sigma_02→Sigma_2 gives injectivity of Sigma_012→Sigma_2. Thus the overworked target in the continued b) line cannot be decided between 02 and 2 by these mathematical consequences.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of the upper-square description, conditional on the same relational/product interpretation and the b) identifications of Sigma_02 and Sigma_12 as subsets of Sigma_2. Their set-theoretic fibre product over Sigma_2 is their intersection. The upper square is Cartesian as a square of sets exactly when its canonical Sigma_012 map identifies Sigma_012 with that intersection, as c) demands. This checks the formulation; it does not derive c) from a) and b), establish topological pullback identifications, or verify bordant, smooth, transversality, or fibration claims. The literal dans Sigma_12 remains unchanged.

Main reader inspected all ten nonidentical independent targets. The lower marginal verb now favors renforcer; the short phrase after Cela remains unresolved. The third upper f) source has a comma in 1,2. Locally incomplete arrowheads and the chevron on the broken central-diagram stroke are recorded from the ink, without changing the conditional mathematical checks in N07–N09.

notes.text: The sheet specifies three topological spaces Sigma_0, Sigma_1, Sigma_2 and closed relations Sigma_01, Sigma_12, Sigma_02. It defines Sigma_012 by an intersection of products, then discusses a commutative diagram, injective/bordante maps, Cartesian squares, transversality and fibration conditions. The two marginal notes interpret the data as an order above [0,1,2] and propose a locally trivial three-object diagram over Sigma_0 as the proposed strengthening/replacement of f), with renforcer preferred and remplacer still possible. The first-reader pass records these source contents. The separate root checks in N07–N09 are conditional and set-theoretic; the geometric conditions d)–f) were not verified.

The first inclusion literally repeats Sigma_01 on both sides. H’s main text changes its right side to Sigma_0 times Sigma_1 and acknowledges that emendation in an editorial note. The literal self-inclusion is retained. The two neighbouring product inclusions and the later definition suggest the intended product, but that is an internal-source inference and is not substituted for the ink.

Condition c) literally states Sigma_012=Sigma_02 intersection Sigma_12 dans Sigma_12. The upper diagram arrows have common target Sigma_2. This comparison distinguishes the written dans Sigma_12 from the common space used to form the intersection after the b) identifications; it does not silently replace the written subscript. The root set-theoretic check is recorded separately in N09.

The continued b) target contains an overworked 0-shaped body before 2. Its state remains undecided between live 02 and a cancelled 0 followed by 2. The later et a fortiori map does not decide that ink. Root’s conditional injectivity check in N08 also shows that both target readings are compatible with the injectivity consequences, so mathematical coherence cannot establish a cancellation.

The singular phrase un morphisme bordant in d), singular fibrant in f), mixed delimiter (liss], and comma in the final Sigma_0,12 index are transcribed literally. The unexplained phrase after Cela remains doubtful, and the missing opening parenthesis is not supplied despite a written closing parenthesis.

This is a single foreground handwritten sheet. No authorial page number or written date is visible at its head. A thin lower-left 7 is recorded as foliation with indeterminate attribution. Apparent isolated W/delta forms in H belong to the complete rotated marginal note; faint show-through/paper specks are not transcribed.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of a), conditional on interpreting Sigma_01 as a relation in Sigma_0 times Sigma_1, and similarly the other Sigma_ij, as indicated by the later triple-product formula and diagram. The literal opening self-inclusion does not itself supply that hypothesis. On the disjoint union, adjoin only identities within each level and the indicated relations between increasing levels. Reflexivity then follows from the adjoined identities, and antisymmetry follows from strictly increasing grades for every nonidentity pair. The only possible composition of two nonidentity pairs is 0→1→2; its transitivity requirement is exactly a), the projection of Sigma_012 to (x0,x2) lying in Sigma_02.

Root targeted injectivity check, under the same relational/product interpretation and a) together with the injection hypotheses in b). Given (x1,x2), the injection Sigma_01→Sigma_1 determines x0, so Sigma_012→Sigma_12 is injective. Given (x0,x2), the injection Sigma_12→Sigma_2 determines x1, so Sigma_012→Sigma_02 is injective. Composing the latter map with the assumed injection Sigma_02→Sigma_2 gives injectivity of Sigma_012→Sigma_2. Thus the overworked target in the continued b) line cannot be decided between 02 and 2 by these mathematical consequences.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of the upper-square description, conditional on the same relational/product interpretation and the b) identifications of Sigma_02 and Sigma_12 as subsets of Sigma_2. Their set-theoretic fibre product over Sigma_2 is their intersection. The upper square is Cartesian as a square of sets exactly when its canonical Sigma_012 map identifies Sigma_012 with that intersection, as c) demands. This checks the formulation; it does not derive c) from a) and b), establish topological pullback identifications, or verify bordant, smooth, transversality, or fibration claims. The literal dans Sigma_12 remains unchanged.

Main reader inspected all ten nonidentical independent targets. The lower marginal verb now favors renforcer; the short phrase after Cela remains unresolved. The third upper f) source has a comma in 1,2. Locally incomplete arrowheads and the chevron on the broken central-diagram stroke are recorded from the ink, without changing the conditional mathematical checks in N07–N09.

notes.text: The foreground of this portrait leaf contains one drawing with six mathematical labels and a separate thin lower-left foliation 9. The broad black diagram ink is distinct from the pale mirrored reverse-side typescript visible through the paper. That show-through, the perforations, stains, folds and loose paper edge are not additional foreground writing. No source prose, title or theorem statement appears on this face. H’s descriptive notes, its comparison with another page and its following section heading are editorial and are not transcribed or used to inspect any other page.

The drawing is reconstructed as an irregular closed oval with three right-going exterior strokes attached at distinct heights. The middle exterior stroke is much thicker and continues the thinner interior radial segment through a filled boundary junction. The interior central point is a vertically elongated filled mark separated from the radial segment by a small actual pen gap; that gap is preserved without inferring that the intended mathematical object is disconnected. The upper-left contour has a short inward return, and the finite drawn ends have no secure arrowheads.

Geometric diagnostic: the only closed path explicitly drawn is the oval contour. The two exterior flank strokes and the middle exterior stroke do not return or connect at their visible ends, so they add no second closed loop. There are two filled geometric points, at the interior marked location and the middle boundary junction. The stars in X_2-star and the central right-hand X_0-star are label characters rather than additional points. This is a check of the depicted incidence and ink, not a verification of a theorem or a definition of the X notation.

The labels use the written indices 0, 1 and 2, including X_{01} beside the middle boundary junction and X_{12} beside each flank stroke. The central equation has two underlined X symbols; the right-hand exterior label also has a clear underline despite its obscured higher/lowered mass. The page supplies no definition of the underline, star or indexed X objects. Their apparent relation to geometric strata is not used to resolve the blackened first zero or to supply a star in the right-hand label.

The original image dimensions are 1708 by 2305 pixels. The whole image and each supplied native half were read once. Four stable crops P01–P04 were created and inspected; no OCR, recognition library, outside research, other page image/witness/report, TeX compilation or recropping was used. All 13 page-specific TSV rows were read as literal tab-separated physical rows. Line_count=6 counts the six written mathematical label units; the separate foliation and picture strokes are not running text lines.

For the right-hand label, an empty-content doubt marker explicitly records a substantial present overtraced group before the final 1; it does not denote a blank. The adjacent TeX comment states that the group extends above/left of 1 and that no cancellation state is established. The outer doubt retains the starred whole-label alternative. This records the ink without drawing a textual symbol as a picture or inventing a deleted zero. The foliation’s possible underline is also marked in place, with underlined 9 preferred to plain 9.

The main reader personally inspected all eight nonidentical second-reading targets. The geometry and clear labels agree. The first obscured zero, blackened right label and foliation underline remain locally uncertain; the second reader’s stronger certainty did not supply missing stroke evidence. No transcription change was made in this audit.

notes.text: The foreground of this portrait leaf contains one drawing with six mathematical labels and a separate thin lower-left foliation 9. The broad black diagram ink is distinct from the pale mirrored reverse-side typescript visible through the paper. That show-through, the perforations, stains, folds and loose paper edge are not additional foreground writing. No source prose, title or theorem statement appears on this face. H’s descriptive notes, its comparison with another page and its following section heading are editorial and are not transcribed or used to inspect any other page.

The drawing is reconstructed as an irregular closed oval with three right-going exterior strokes attached at distinct heights. The middle exterior stroke is much thicker and continues the thinner interior radial segment through a filled boundary junction. The interior central point is a vertically elongated filled mark separated from the radial segment by a small actual pen gap; that gap is preserved without inferring that the intended mathematical object is disconnected. The upper-left contour has a short inward return, and the finite drawn ends have no secure arrowheads.

Geometric diagnostic: the only closed path explicitly drawn is the oval contour. The two exterior flank strokes and the middle exterior stroke do not return or connect at their visible ends, so they add no second closed loop. There are two filled geometric points, at the interior marked location and the middle boundary junction. The stars in X_2-star and the central right-hand X_0-star are label characters rather than additional points. This is a check of the depicted incidence and ink, not a verification of a theorem or a definition of the X notation.

The labels use the written indices 0, 1 and 2, including X_{01} beside the middle boundary junction and X_{12} beside each flank stroke. The central equation has two underlined X symbols; the right-hand exterior label also has a clear underline despite its obscured higher/lowered mass. The page supplies no definition of the underline, star or indexed X objects. Their apparent relation to geometric strata is not used to resolve the blackened first zero or to supply a star in the right-hand label.

The original image dimensions are 1708 by 2305 pixels. The whole image and each supplied native half were read once. Four stable crops P01–P04 were created and inspected; no OCR, recognition library, outside research, other page image/witness/report, TeX compilation or recropping was used. All 13 page-specific TSV rows were read as literal tab-separated physical rows. Line_count=6 counts the six written mathematical label units; the separate foliation and picture strokes are not running text lines.

For the right-hand label, an empty-content doubt marker explicitly records a substantial present overtraced group before the final 1; it does not denote a blank. The adjacent TeX comment states that the group extends above/left of 1 and that no cancellation state is established. The outer doubt retains the starred whole-label alternative. This records the ink without drawing a textual symbol as a picture or inventing a deleted zero. The foliation’s possible underline is also marked in place, with underlined 9 preferred to plain 9.

The main reader personally inspected all eight nonidentical second-reading targets. The geometry and clear labels agree. The first obscured zero, blackened right label and foliation underline remain locally uncertain; the second reader’s stronger certainty did not supply missing stroke evidence. No transcription change was made in this audit.

notes.text: Source report: the title replaces “tubulaires” by “coniques”. The page defines a “voisinage conique” (also “cône sur Y”) using a space T containing Y, a closed part dot T, and an action of the multiplicative interval monoid I=[0,1]. The source axioms a), b), c), the starred pushout explanation, the canonical-map identifications and the final interior formula are transcribed. This description by itself is not a proof check. No outside source was used.

Main-reader targeted deduction, communicated by root and retained as a check: a) and b), together with the continuous unital I-action, imply a strong deformation retraction of T onto Y. Let r(t)=0t and H(s,t)=(1-s)t. Then H(0,t)=t, H(1,t)=r(t) is in Y by b), and H(s,y)=y by a). In particular r(y)=y. This explains the right marginal “sur une rétraction” without adding words to it.

Main-reader targeted deduction: the weaker condition 0.dot T subset Y, together with a) and the cocartesian square c), implies b). In the pushout every point has a representative y in Y or lambda b with b in dot T. For y, 0y=y by a); for lambda b, the action law gives 0(lambda b)=(0 lambda)b=0b in Y. This verifies the intended marginal implication. The written NB nonetheless ends at “entraînent”: the parenthesized token is kept once at the diagram position as (2)|(b), not supplied as the verb’s missing object.

Main-reader targeted deduction: the pushout identifies the whole copy {0}×dot T with its image in Y and makes no other identifications between Y and (0,1]×dot T. Thus the latter points and Y form the disjoint representative description. The source star-note bijection from I_{]0,1]}×dot T to T minus Y is consistent with that quotient description. It does not establish that this bijection is a homeomorphism, and the transcription does not add such a statement.

Main-reader targeted deduction for the final equation: using the representative description, the union of lambda T for 0≤lambda<1 is Y union ((0,1)×dot T), hence T minus dot T. One inclusion follows because multiplying a representative with positive parameter by lambda<1 yields parameter below 1. Conversely, a parameter mu<1 is mu times a parameter-1 representative, and Y is fixed. This verifies the equation defining the interior and explains how the action determines the boundary as its complement.

Main-reader targeted quotient-topology check: a subset of the pushout is open exactly when its inverse images in Y and I×dot T are open. Root audit of the enlarged rotated note resolves the visible continuation as inverses/inverse dans I×dot T et dans Y le sont; the final predicate is present in the ink. The previous draft claim that it was missing is withdrawn. This independently recovered wording agrees with the quotient-topology check; the check itself did not supply the reading. The crossed label above bij. is recorded separately as doubtful homéo.

Possible author slip / unresolved letter in (3): the argument of f looks like a closed a rather than the crossed x used on the right of 0.x. Both witnesses print f(x)=0.x. The diplomatic text retains f(a|x)=0.x with a preferred. Mathematical consistency would favor using x on both sides, but the check does not settle the letter against the ink.

Notation and geometry are kept literal. The T forms have single roofs; bold serif I was checked locally, including all five occurrences in the middle action paragraph P28. The main square has four objects, four shafts, six heads and one hook, counted twice. Later situation connectors have outer hooks but no secure central heads; their intended inclusion/map interpretations do not supply those heads. The colon after “isomorphe”, the unmatched extra closing quotation after tube, the source Le before the cancelled application, and the incomplete NB ending are preserved; the star note has a visible final le sont.

Reading record: the assigned original was viewed once, both supplied native halves once, and each saved first-pass crop P00–P26 once. P27 was authorized specifically for the still-open original-orientation attachment of the number/NB ending. Only the still-open rétraction ending was then consulted in saved P11; no new crop of a decided place was made. P28 is the first crop of the previously uncropped action paragraph, to check local I weight. There were no OCR, recognition libraries, outside research, compilation, other-page images, or other-page reports. Root independently reviewed all 29 crops.

The faint narrow lower-left 11 is retained separately from the large author folio 1). Its hand is not attributed with certainty from line weight alone. Punctuation at the physically clipped right edge is explicitly uncertain. Pale substrate/stain marks were not transcribed as text.

Independent second-reading audit: root personally inspected every nonidentical box, plus targeted enlarged portions of the homotopy/star notes and wider original-image crops for B24 and B29. B24 clipped the dot above T; B29 covered Soit rather than the circled 1. The fixed first and second readings are preserved, and final changes are recorded separately.

notes.text: Source report: the title replaces “tubulaires” by “coniques”. The page defines a “voisinage conique” (also “cône sur Y”) using a space T containing Y, a closed part dot T, and an action of the multiplicative interval monoid I=[0,1]. The source axioms a), b), c), the starred pushout explanation, the canonical-map identifications and the final interior formula are transcribed. This description by itself is not a proof check. No outside source was used.

Main-reader targeted deduction, communicated by root and retained as a check: a) and b), together with the continuous unital I-action, imply a strong deformation retraction of T onto Y. Let r(t)=0t and H(s,t)=(1-s)t. Then H(0,t)=t, H(1,t)=r(t) is in Y by b), and H(s,y)=y by a). In particular r(y)=y. This explains the right marginal “sur une rétraction” without adding words to it.

Main-reader targeted deduction: the weaker condition 0.dot T subset Y, together with a) and the cocartesian square c), implies b). In the pushout every point has a representative y in Y or lambda b with b in dot T. For y, 0y=y by a); for lambda b, the action law gives 0(lambda b)=(0 lambda)b=0b in Y. This verifies the intended marginal implication. The written NB nonetheless ends at “entraînent”: the parenthesized token is kept once at the diagram position as (2)|(b), not supplied as the verb’s missing object.

Main-reader targeted deduction: the pushout identifies the whole copy {0}×dot T with its image in Y and makes no other identifications between Y and (0,1]×dot T. Thus the latter points and Y form the disjoint representative description. The source star-note bijection from I_{]0,1]}×dot T to T minus Y is consistent with that quotient description. It does not establish that this bijection is a homeomorphism, and the transcription does not add such a statement.

Main-reader targeted deduction for the final equation: using the representative description, the union of lambda T for 0≤lambda<1 is Y union ((0,1)×dot T), hence T minus dot T. One inclusion follows because multiplying a representative with positive parameter by lambda<1 yields parameter below 1. Conversely, a parameter mu<1 is mu times a parameter-1 representative, and Y is fixed. This verifies the equation defining the interior and explains how the action determines the boundary as its complement.

Main-reader targeted quotient-topology check: a subset of the pushout is open exactly when its inverse images in Y and I×dot T are open. Root audit of the enlarged rotated note resolves the visible continuation as inverses/inverse dans I×dot T et dans Y le sont; the final predicate is present in the ink. The previous draft claim that it was missing is withdrawn. This independently recovered wording agrees with the quotient-topology check; the check itself did not supply the reading. The crossed label above bij. is recorded separately as doubtful homéo.

Possible author slip / unresolved letter in (3): the argument of f looks like a closed a rather than the crossed x used on the right of 0.x. Both witnesses print f(x)=0.x. The diplomatic text retains f(a|x)=0.x with a preferred. Mathematical consistency would favor using x on both sides, but the check does not settle the letter against the ink.

Notation and geometry are kept literal. The T forms have single roofs; bold serif I was checked locally, including all five occurrences in the middle action paragraph P28. The main square has four objects, four shafts, six heads and one hook, counted twice. Later situation connectors have outer hooks but no secure central heads; their intended inclusion/map interpretations do not supply those heads. The colon after “isomorphe”, the unmatched extra closing quotation after tube, the source Le before the cancelled application, and the incomplete NB ending are preserved; the star note has a visible final le sont.

Reading record: the assigned original was viewed once, both supplied native halves once, and each saved first-pass crop P00–P26 once. P27 was authorized specifically for the still-open original-orientation attachment of the number/NB ending. Only the still-open rétraction ending was then consulted in saved P11; no new crop of a decided place was made. P28 is the first crop of the previously uncropped action paragraph, to check local I weight. There were no OCR, recognition libraries, outside research, compilation, other-page images, or other-page reports. Root independently reviewed all 29 crops.

The faint narrow lower-left 11 is retained separately from the large author folio 1). Its hand is not attributed with certainty from line weight alone. The canonical-map formula ends in source f without parentheses; no hypothetical punctuation beyond the physically clipped right edge is supplied. Pale substrate/stain marks were not transcribed as text.

Independent second-reading audit: root personally inspected every nonidentical box, plus targeted enlarged portions of the homotopy/star notes and wider original-image crops for B24 and B29. B24 clipped the dot above T; B29 covered Soit rather than the circled 1. The fixed first and second readings are preserved, and final changes are recorded separately.

The hollow-circle and filled-dot forms supply local comparisons. The written empty set is phi. Prose E_epsilon and displayed Ep_epsilon coexist and are preserved. Inverse rotation maps the apparent blob after forment to the current formula number (6), about original (245,1062), and the alleged T_epsilon after voisinages to the main-text underlined NB, about (269,1351). Those elements are transcribed once in the main text, not duplicated as marginal cancellations. The final assertion reads “est la frontière de T_lambda [=|:] lambda T dans X”. Both inline map connectors lack a secure arrowhead. Root targeted counterexample, conditional on the cone-action interpretation supplied by root from the preceding page (not independently read by this first reader): take X=([0,1]×{0}) union ({1/2}×[0,1]), T=[0,1]×{0}, Y={(0,0)}, dotted T={(1,0)}, and lambda·(t,0)=(lambda t,0). T is closed in X and contains a neighbourhood of Y; it is the cone on dotted T→Y. At lambda=3/4, T_lambda=[0,3/4]×{0}. Its ambient boundary in X consists of the junction (1/2,0) and the endpoint (3/4,0), whereas lambda dotted T consists only of (3/4,0). Thus the final ambient-frontier assertion fails under these hypotheses. Root confirmed the exact final ink in P10 before this diagnostic was added. The transcription is unchanged.

Refinement of N05: the issue is the distinction between the interior in T and the ambient interior in X. In the counterexample, the junction belongs to the former but not the latter. An additional hypothesis controlling ambient openness of the cone interior would be needed to exclude this obstruction; no general sufficiency theorem is asserted here. This check does not verify the compactness/fundamental-system marginal claim or all preceding cone identities.

Footer scope check: the final lambda meets the physical sheet edge. Completing strip P12 contains only that edge and black scanner background below it; it adds no source letters or indices. No diagram or unrelated drawing occurs on this leaf; the two marginal vertical strokes and the unheaded inline connectors are retained as written symbols.

Root targeted proof check, under the canonical cone/pushout model of the preceding leaf: T is the quotient of Y disjoint-union ([0,1] times dotted T), identifying (0,b) with f(b). For 0<lambda<=1, T_lambda has inverse image Y disjoint-union ([0,lambda] times dotted T), hence is closed by the quotient topology. The circled T_lambda has inverse image Y disjoint-union ([0,lambda[ times dotted T), hence is open. If 0<lambda<1, every point (lambda,b) has arbitrarily close radial points with larger parameter; thus the interior in T of T_lambda is exactly circled T_lambda. At lambda=1 the interior of T in itself is all T, explaining the stated endpoint exception. These arguments use the canonical pushout interpretation, not the literal extra arrowheads in the preceding diagram.

Root targeted proof check, with 0<epsilon<1 and lambda=1-epsilon: the part of the cone away from Y is homeomorphic to ]0,1] times dotted T. Hence E_epsilon=T minus circled T_lambda is [lambda,1] times dotted T, a neighbourhood of dotted T, with frontier in T equal to {lambda} times dotted T. The separately defined dotted Ep includes both endpoint copies; it need not equal that ambient frontier. If Y and dotted T are compact, the defining disjoint union is compact and so is its quotient T. For any open neighbourhood V of Y, its inverse image contains {0} times dotted T; compactness of dotted T and the tube lemma give a uniform delta>0 with [0,delta] times dotted T mapped into V. Thus the scaled T_delta form a neighbourhood basis. Compactness of Y is not needed for this last basis assertion.

Root targeted qualification of the marginal revision fermés to ouverts: with T_epsilon interpreted as the scaled closed subsets defined in the main text, they are not generally open. In the cone on a point, T=[0,1], Y={0}, dotted T={1}, and T_epsilon=[0,epsilon]; for 0<epsilon<1 this is closed and a neighbourhood of Y but not open in T. The circled T_epsilon=[0,epsilon[ are open. The marginal word ouverts, now with an uncertain d’ prefix, is nevertheless retained because its letters and insertion state are visible; the unclear extra fragment plus/plein : T might bear on the intended attachment, which is not imposed here.
