notes.text: This double manuscript leaf, authorial pages 3 and 4), develops conditions on a locally finite indexed pseudo-partition and its map phi to a preordered set: continuity, final/quotient topology, openness, and non-emptiness. It then describes strict stratifications by increasing closed families, intersections, and the condition that X_j be rare in X_i when j<i. These are contents of the source, transcribed without a theorem proof.

The left condition 3 literally reads bar X_j* = union over j≤i of X_j*, followed by pour tt j in I. The same handwritten j is clear in the left subscript and final quantifier, while the bound ends in i. This free/bound-index mismatch is preserved. The source forms were compared with the nearby definition X_i=union over j≤i X_j*; the comparison identifies a local notation discrepancy and does not license emendation.

The left separation criterion ends with the literal les X_i sont loc. fermés, without stars. Earlier the same page assumes the X_i closed, whereas the later right paragraph explicitly refers to X_i* being locally closed. This internal source comparison flags the missing-star possibility for mathematical review, but the unstarred written X_i remains in the transcription. No proof of the asserted equivalence was attempted.

The vertical déf annotation below X_i* gives X_i minus the union over j<i of X_j, with no star on its summand. The later Moyennant sentence explicitly uses X_j* in that union. Both forms are retained; no equivalence is supplied by editorial emendation.

The lower-left discussion is framed by il faut voir comment and concerns a least moderate strict refinement of a partition by locally closed moderate pieces. The author’s question and the revisions after plus petite are preserved, including unresolved state and plurality of the raised strictes. This is not presented as a verified existence theorem.

The landscape sheet has a central pen divider, two slanted left separator strokes and a horizontal left separator. The isolated upper-right group is written at 180 degrees to the main text and is reproduced upright, preserving uncertain J/I and upper symbols. The authorial numbers are 3 and 4); a thinner lower-left 3 has indeterminate attribution. No date is visible. Pale reversed/show-through matter is excluded.

The quotient criterion has an extra closing parenthesis after X_L* ouvert. In the right uniqueness display the first closing mark is brace-like and remains qualified as brace/parenthesis; the next equivalence has separate parentheses. Curved leaders at loc. finie, croissante, stratifiantes and pour l’ordre donné à I are not separate underlines or parentheses. Fermées has an independent underline.

Openness criterion: For a continuous map f, openness is equivalent to f^{-1}(closure B) = closure(f^{-1}(B)) for all B. Continuity supplies the inclusion from the right to the left. Openness supplies the reverse: any neighborhood U of x maps to a neighborhood f(U) of f(x), so f(x) in closure B forces U to meet f^{-1}(B). Conversely this reverse inclusion implies every f(U) is open: if a point y in f(U) were in closure(Y\f(U)), an x in U over y would be in closure(f^{-1}(Y\f(U))), contradicting the open neighborhood U. These checks do not change the source j/i mismatch in its numbered formula.

Local closedness diagnostic: The source identifies each cumulative X_i with a closed union of strata. Such an X_i is automatically locally closed, so the written parenthetical criterion using X_i without a star cannot by itself characterize antisymmetry of the quotient preorder. The intended criterion plausibly concerns X_i^*, but the unstarred ink is retained. This is a diagnostic of the written definitions, not an emendation.

The 3 bis note: Under the page's conditions1,2,4 and local finiteness, the equivalence between nonempty X_i and nonempty X_i^* can be checked locally. The lower closed subsets X_j (j<i) are nowhere dense in X_i under condition4; only finitely many are present near any chosen point by local finiteness. A finite union of closed nowhere dense subsets cannot cover a nonempty open piece of X_i. Thus a nonempty X_i has a point outside their union. This validates the conditional argument of the note without changing its labels or uncertain glyphs.

Independent-reading scope check: B13 clipped the opening quantifier, and B33 clipped most of the intersection formula. The main reader inspected wider original crops P10wide and P25wide and retained those readings. The fixed second reading is not altered. The upright marginal diagram was a substantive orientation correction.

notes.text: The sheet specifies three topological spaces Sigma_0, Sigma_1, Sigma_2 and closed relations Sigma_01, Sigma_12, Sigma_02. It defines Sigma_012 by an intersection of products, then discusses a commutative diagram, injective/bordante maps, Cartesian squares, transversality and fibration conditions. The two marginal notes interpret the data as an order above [0,1,2] and propose a locally trivial three-object diagram over Sigma_0 as the proposed strengthening/replacement of f), with renforcer preferred and remplacer still possible. The first-reader pass records these source contents. The separate root checks in N07–N09 are conditional and set-theoretic; the geometric conditions d)–f) were not verified.

The first inclusion literally repeats Sigma_01 on both sides. H’s main text changes its right side to Sigma_0 times Sigma_1 and acknowledges that emendation in an editorial note. The literal self-inclusion is retained. The two neighbouring product inclusions and the later definition suggest the intended product, but that is an internal-source inference and is not substituted for the ink.

Condition c) literally states Sigma_012=Sigma_02 intersection Sigma_12 dans Sigma_12. The upper diagram arrows have common target Sigma_2. This comparison distinguishes the written dans Sigma_12 from the common space used to form the intersection after the b) identifications; it does not silently replace the written subscript. The root set-theoretic check is recorded separately in N09.

The continued b) target contains an overworked 0-shaped body before 2. Its state remains undecided between live 02 and a cancelled 0 followed by 2. The later et a fortiori map does not decide that ink. Root’s conditional injectivity check in N08 also shows that both target readings are compatible with the injectivity consequences, so mathematical coherence cannot establish a cancellation.

The singular phrase un morphisme bordant in d), singular fibrant in f), mixed delimiter (liss], and comma in the final Sigma_0,12 index are transcribed literally. The unexplained phrase after Cela remains doubtful, and the missing opening parenthesis is not supplied despite a written closing parenthesis.

This is a single foreground handwritten sheet. No authorial page number or written date is visible at its head. A thin lower-left 7 is recorded as foliation with indeterminate attribution. Apparent isolated W/delta forms in H belong to the complete rotated marginal note; faint show-through/paper specks are not transcribed.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of a), conditional on interpreting Sigma_01 as a relation in Sigma_0 times Sigma_1, and similarly the other Sigma_ij, as indicated by the later triple-product formula and diagram. The literal opening self-inclusion does not itself supply that hypothesis. On the disjoint union, adjoin only identities within each level and the indicated relations between increasing levels. Reflexivity then follows from the adjoined identities, and antisymmetry follows from strictly increasing grades for every nonidentity pair. The only possible composition of two nonidentity pairs is 0→1→2; its transitivity requirement is exactly a), the projection of Sigma_012 to (x0,x2) lying in Sigma_02.

Root targeted injectivity check, under the same relational/product interpretation and a) together with the injection hypotheses in b). Given (x1,x2), the injection Sigma_01→Sigma_1 determines x0, so Sigma_012→Sigma_12 is injective. Given (x0,x2), the injection Sigma_12→Sigma_2 determines x1, so Sigma_012→Sigma_02 is injective. Composing the latter map with the assumed injection Sigma_02→Sigma_2 gives injectivity of Sigma_012→Sigma_2. Thus the overworked target in the continued b) line cannot be decided between 02 and 2 by these mathematical consequences.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of the upper-square description, conditional on the same relational/product interpretation and the b) identifications of Sigma_02 and Sigma_12 as subsets of Sigma_2. Their set-theoretic fibre product over Sigma_2 is their intersection. The upper square is Cartesian as a square of sets exactly when its canonical Sigma_012 map identifies Sigma_012 with that intersection, as c) demands. This checks the formulation; it does not derive c) from a) and b), establish topological pullback identifications, or verify bordant, smooth, transversality, or fibration claims. The literal dans Sigma_12 remains unchanged.

Main reader inspected all ten nonidentical independent targets. The lower marginal verb now favors renforcer; the short phrase after Cela remains unresolved. The third upper f) source has a comma in 1,2. Locally incomplete arrowheads and the chevron on the broken central-diagram stroke are recorded from the ink, without changing the conditional mathematical checks in N07–N09.

notes.text: The sheet specifies three topological spaces Sigma_0, Sigma_1, Sigma_2 and closed relations Sigma_01, Sigma_12, Sigma_02. It defines Sigma_012 by an intersection of products, then discusses a commutative diagram, injective/bordante maps, Cartesian squares, transversality and fibration conditions. The two marginal notes interpret the data as an order above [0,1,2] and propose a locally trivial three-object diagram over Sigma_0 as the proposed strengthening/replacement of f), with renforcer preferred and remplacer still possible. The first-reader pass records these source contents. The separate root checks in N07–N09 are conditional and set-theoretic; the geometric conditions d)–f) were not verified.

The first inclusion literally repeats Sigma_01 on both sides. H’s main text changes its right side to Sigma_0 times Sigma_1 and acknowledges that emendation in an editorial note. The literal self-inclusion is retained. The two neighbouring product inclusions and the later definition suggest the intended product, but that is an internal-source inference and is not substituted for the ink.

Condition c) literally states Sigma_012=Sigma_02 intersection Sigma_12 dans Sigma_12. The upper diagram arrows have common target Sigma_2. This comparison distinguishes the written dans Sigma_12 from the common space used to form the intersection after the b) identifications; it does not silently replace the written subscript. The root set-theoretic check is recorded separately in N09.

The continued b) target contains an overworked 0-shaped body before 2. Its state remains undecided between live 02 and a cancelled 0 followed by 2. The later et a fortiori map does not decide that ink. Root’s conditional injectivity check in N08 also shows that both target readings are compatible with the injectivity consequences, so mathematical coherence cannot establish a cancellation.

The singular phrase un morphisme bordant in d), singular fibrant in f), mixed delimiter (liss], and comma in the final Sigma_0,12 index are transcribed literally. The unexplained phrase after Cela remains doubtful, and the missing opening parenthesis is not supplied despite a written closing parenthesis.

This is a single foreground handwritten sheet. No authorial page number or written date is visible at its head. A thin lower-left 7 is recorded as foliation with indeterminate attribution. Apparent isolated W/delta forms in H belong to the complete rotated marginal note; faint show-through/paper specks are not transcribed.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of a), conditional on interpreting Sigma_01 as a relation in Sigma_0 times Sigma_1, and similarly the other Sigma_ij, as indicated by the later triple-product formula and diagram. The literal opening self-inclusion does not itself supply that hypothesis. On the disjoint union, adjoin only identities within each level and the indicated relations between increasing levels. Reflexivity then follows from the adjoined identities, and antisymmetry follows from strictly increasing grades for every nonidentity pair. The only possible composition of two nonidentity pairs is 0→1→2; its transitivity requirement is exactly a), the projection of Sigma_012 to (x0,x2) lying in Sigma_02.

Root targeted injectivity check, under the same relational/product interpretation and a) together with the injection hypotheses in b). Given (x1,x2), the injection Sigma_01→Sigma_1 determines x0, so Sigma_012→Sigma_12 is injective. Given (x0,x2), the injection Sigma_12→Sigma_2 determines x1, so Sigma_012→Sigma_02 is injective. Composing the latter map with the assumed injection Sigma_02→Sigma_2 gives injectivity of Sigma_012→Sigma_2. Thus the overworked target in the continued b) line cannot be decided between 02 and 2 by these mathematical consequences.

Root targeted set-theoretic check of the upper-square description, conditional on the same relational/product interpretation and the b) identifications of Sigma_02 and Sigma_12 as subsets of Sigma_2. Their set-theoretic fibre product over Sigma_2 is their intersection. The upper square is Cartesian as a square of sets exactly when its canonical Sigma_012 map identifies Sigma_012 with that intersection, as c) demands. This checks the formulation; it does not derive c) from a) and b), establish topological pullback identifications, or verify bordant, smooth, transversality, or fibration claims. The literal dans Sigma_12 remains unchanged.

Main reader inspected all ten nonidentical independent targets. The lower marginal verb now favors renforcer; the short phrase after Cela remains unresolved. The third upper f) source has a comma in 1,2. Locally incomplete arrowheads and the chevron on the broken central-diagram stroke are recorded from the ink, without changing the conditional mathematical checks in N07–N09.

notes.text: The foreground of this portrait leaf contains one drawing with six mathematical labels and a separate thin lower-left foliation 9. The broad black diagram ink is distinct from the pale mirrored reverse-side typescript visible through the paper. That show-through, the perforations, stains, folds and loose paper edge are not additional foreground writing. No source prose, title or theorem statement appears on this face. H’s descriptive notes, its comparison with another page and its following section heading are editorial and are not transcribed or used to inspect any other page.

The drawing is reconstructed as an irregular closed oval with three right-going exterior strokes attached at distinct heights. The middle exterior stroke is much thicker and continues the thinner interior radial segment through a filled boundary junction. The interior central point is a vertically elongated filled mark separated from the radial segment by a small actual pen gap; that gap is preserved without inferring that the intended mathematical object is disconnected. The upper-left contour has a short inward return, and the finite drawn ends have no secure arrowheads.

Geometric diagnostic: the only closed path explicitly drawn is the oval contour. The two exterior flank strokes and the middle exterior stroke do not return or connect at their visible ends, so they add no second closed loop. There are two filled geometric points, at the interior marked location and the middle boundary junction. The stars in X_2-star and the central right-hand X_0-star are label characters rather than additional points. This is a check of the depicted incidence and ink, not a verification of a theorem or a definition of the X notation.

The labels use the written indices 0, 1 and 2, including X_{01} beside the middle boundary junction and X_{12} beside each flank stroke. Source and notation check: all ordinary T forms on this leaf have a single cap and stem; C’s repeated bars are not supported by a second horizontal stroke. The hollow-circle and filled-dot forms supply local comparisons. The written empty set is phi. Prose E_epsilon and displayed Ep_epsilon coexist and are preserved. Inverse rotation maps the apparent blob after forment to the current formula number (6), about original (245,1062), and the alleged T_epsilon after voisinages to the main-text underlined NB, about (269,1351). Those elements are transcribed once in the main text, not duplicated as marginal cancellations. The source retains the literal word “tubulaires” in the final family paragraph after the earlier inserted replacement coniq. for cancelled tub. The final assertion reads “est la frontière de T_lambda [=|:] lambda T dans X”. Both inline map connectors lack a secure arrowhead. The old (6), current (6), and final (8) show overwork; no invented chronological sequence or earlier numeral is supplied. Thin foliation 12 has indeterminate attribution.

Root targeted counterexample, conditional on the cone-action interpretation supplied by root from the preceding page (not independently read by this first reader): take X=([0,1]×{0}) union ({1/2}×[0,1]), T=[0,1]×{0}, Y={(0,0)}, dotted T={(1,0)}, and lambda·(t,0)=(lambda t,0). T is closed in X and contains a neighbourhood of Y; it is the cone on dotted T→Y. At lambda=3/4, T_lambda=[0,3/4]×{0}. Its ambient boundary in X consists of the junction (1/2,0) and the endpoint (3/4,0), whereas lambda dotted T consists only of (3/4,0). Thus the final ambient-frontier assertion fails under these hypotheses. Root confirmed the exact final ink in P10 before this diagnostic was added. The transcription is unchanged.

Refinement of N05: the issue is the distinction between the interior in T and the ambient interior in X. In the counterexample, the junction belongs to the former but not the latter. An additional hypothesis controlling ambient openness of the cone interior would be needed to exclude this obstruction; no general sufficiency theorem is asserted here. This check does not verify the compactness/fundamental-system marginal claim or all preceding cone identities.

Footer scope check: the final lambda meets the physical sheet edge. Completing strip P12 contains only that edge and black scanner background below it; it adds no source letters or indices. No diagram or unrelated drawing occurs on this leaf; the two marginal vertical strokes and the unheaded inline connectors are retained as written symbols.

Root targeted proof check, under the canonical cone/pushout model of the preceding leaf: T is the quotient of Y disjoint-union ([0,1] times dotted T), identifying (0,b) with f(b). For 0<lambda<=1, T_lambda has inverse image Y disjoint-union ([0,lambda] times dotted T), hence is closed by the quotient topology. The circled T_lambda has inverse image Y disjoint-union ([0,lambda[ times dotted T), hence is open. If 0<lambda<1, every point (lambda,b) has arbitrarily close radial points with larger parameter; thus the interior in T of T_lambda is exactly circled T_lambda. At lambda=1 the interior of T in itself is all T, explaining the stated endpoint exception. These arguments use the canonical pushout interpretation, not the literal extra arrowheads in the preceding diagram.

Root targeted proof check, with 0<epsilon<1 and lambda=1-epsilon: the part of the cone away from Y is homeomorphic to ]0,1] times dotted T. Hence E_epsilon=T minus circled T_lambda is [lambda,1] times dotted T, a neighbourhood of dotted T, with frontier in T equal to {lambda} times dotted T. The separately defined dotted Ep includes both endpoint copies; it need not equal that ambient frontier. If Y and dotted T are compact, the defining disjoint union is compact and so is its quotient T. For any open neighbourhood V of Y, its inverse image contains {0} times dotted T; compactness of dotted T and the tube lemma give a uniform delta>0 with [0,delta] times dotted T mapped into V. Thus the scaled T_delta form a neighbourhood basis. Compactness of Y is not needed for this last basis assertion.

Root targeted qualification of the marginal revision fermés to ouverts: with T_epsilon interpreted as the scaled closed subsets defined in the main text, they are not generally open. In the cone on a point, T=[0,1], Y={0}, dotted T={1}, and T_epsilon=[0,epsilon]; for 0<epsilon<1 this is closed and a neighbourhood of Y but not open in T. The circled T_epsilon=[0,epsilon[ are open. The marginal word ouverts, now with an uncertain d’ prefix, is nevertheless retained because its letters and insertion state are visible; the unclear extra fragment plus/plein : T might bear on the intended attachment, which is not imposed here.

Independent audit: root inspected all 11 nonidentical boxes, then the native page and targeted margin/formula enlargements. The overlap of the margin with the main formula number and NB was explicitly checked, preventing duplicate transcription of those neighbouring elements. Five boxes have revised final records; fixed independent readings are unchanged.

Root targeted counterexample, conditional on the cone-action interpretation supplied by root from the preceding page (not independently read by this first reader): take X=([0,1]×{0}) union ({1/2}×[0,1]), T=[0,1]×{0}, Y={(0,0)}, dotted T={(1,0)}, and lambda·(t,0)=(lambda t,0). T is closed in X and contains a neighbourhood of Y; it is the cone on dotted T→Y. At lambda=3/4, T_lambda=[0,3/4]×{0}. Its ambient boundary in X consists of the junction (1/2,0) and the endpoint (3/4,0), whereas lambda dotted T consists only of (3/4,0). Thus the final ambient-frontier assertion fails under these hypotheses. Root confirmed the exact final ink in P10 before this diagnostic was added. The transcription is unchanged.

Refinement of N05: the issue is the distinction between the interior in T and the ambient interior in X. In the counterexample, the junction belongs to the former but not the latter. An additional hypothesis controlling ambient openness of the cone interior would be needed to exclude this obstruction; no general sufficiency theorem is asserted here. This check does not verify the compactness/fundamental-system marginal claim or all preceding cone identities.

No diagram or unrelated drawing occurs on this leaf; the two marginal vertical strokes and the unheaded inline connectors are retained as written symbols.

Root targeted proof check, under the canonical cone/pushout model of the preceding leaf: T is the quotient of Y disjoint-union ([0,1] times dotted T), identifying (0,b) with f(b). For 0<lambda<=1, T_lambda has inverse image Y disjoint-union ([0,lambda] times dotted T), hence is closed by the quotient topology. The circled T_lambda has inverse image Y disjoint-union ([0,lambda[ times dotted T), hence is open. If 0<lambda<1, every point (lambda,b) has arbitrarily close radial points with larger parameter; thus the interior in T of T_lambda is exactly circled T_lambda. At lambda=1 the interior of T in itself is all T, explaining the stated endpoint exception. notes.text: The sheet is manuscript text in his hand, with author number 2), a diagonal left-margin note, two mathematical diagram blocks, numerous revisions, and thin lower-left foliation 13 in another or undetermined hand. The entire original and both supplied native halves were read once; all fifteen saved crops were inspected once. P10 is rotated 45 degrees clockwise for reading, while every recorded coordinate remains in the original 1685 by 2363 image. The main text has nineteen physical prose lines, one equality display and one triangular diagram block (line_count 21 by this convention); the diagonal margin is inventoried separately. H’s foliation discussion, note about its added vertical arrow and proposed famille correction are editorial, not manuscript text.

Targeted boundary check. The source says “Mais on ne peut pas dire … en général que dot T soit la frontière de T dans X” and gives X=T with dot T not equal to the written 0. For any space X, the topological boundary of X inside itself is closure_X(X) minus interior_X(X), hence empty. Taking a nonempty Y and X=T=Y×[0,1], with the distinguished outer section dot T=Y×{1}, gives a nonempty dot T and empty ambient frontier. Thus the displayed counterexample mechanism is valid. This checks that mechanism only: reference (7) is read from its ink and the unavailable earlier statement numbered (7) is not reconstructed. The source’s un-crossed oval 0 is retained, not silently changed to phi or an empty-set glyph.

Independent local re-proof of the collar/mapping-cylinder equivalence, conditional on cônique having its usual mapping-cylinder meaning here. Let f:B→Y be a homeomorphism and let C(f) be the quotient of Y disjoint union (B×[0,1]) by (b,0) identified with f(b). The map sending the base y to (y,0) and the class of (b,r) to (f(b),r) is well-defined and continuous by the quotient property. Its inverse sends (y,r) to the class of (f^{-1}(y),r); this is continuous and agrees with the base identification at r=0. The two maps compose to the identities, so C(f)≃Y×[0,1] and the base inclusion becomes y↦(y,0), precisely the commutativity of diagram (10). Conversely a product collar transports the identity-map cone structure on Y×[0,1]. This proof uses an explicitly stated interpretation of the cone construction; the assigned leaf does not define all of its earlier notation. No extra bar on T is justified by this interpretation.

Targeted check of the absolute-cone and strip examples. Under the standard radial convention, away from the cone vertex the absolute cone on B has the product coordinates B×(0,1]. For any 0<a<1, the strip B×[a,1] is a collar neighborhood of the outer section B×{1}; the coordinate u=(1-r)/(1-a) sends that section to u=0 and gives B×[0,1]. For a positive radius lambda, the same construction on [a lambda,lambda] collars the section B×{lambda} inside the truncated cone T_lambda. This requires lambda>0; the source’s line does not state its range anew, and no assertion about the vertex radius zero is inferred. For a product strip B×[a,b] with a<b, each endpoint section has a collar obtained by a sufficiently short endpoint subinterval. Their union has a collar by choosing two disjoint endpoint subintervals and taking the disjoint union of those product collars. Therefore the three listed boundary choices are valid if the live barred-E-p operator denotes that radial strip and 0<epsilon<1. The operator is not defined on this leaf, so that identification and parameter range remain explicit hypotheses, not purported recovered definitions. The first epsilon/delta/lambda reading remains unresolved despite the expected strip formula.

Independent re-proof of the closing finite-union statement under the compact-Hausdorff convention, and assuming the uncertain lower J/I denotes the same finite index set as the preceding family. Let Y_i be finitely many pairwise disjoint closed subsets of compact Hausdorff X, and write Y for their union. Each Y_i is clopen in Y. If h:Y×[0,1]→T is a collar with h(y,0)=y and T a neighborhood of Y, then h(Y_i×[0,1]) is a neighborhood of Y_i: its product component is open in T, and intersecting it with an ambient open neighborhood of Y contained in T gives an ambient open neighborhood of Y_i. The restricted h is its collar. Conversely choose pairwise disjoint ambient open neighborhoods U_i of the Y_i, using normality for a finite family. For a collar h_i:Y_i×[0,1]→T_i, the preimage of U_i∩T_i is open and contains the compact zero section Y_i×{0}. A finite subcover by product neighborhoods provides delta_i>0 such that h_i(Y_i×[0,delta_i]) lies in U_i. Each shortened strip is still a neighborhood of Y_i: the smaller relatively open product Y_i×[0,delta_i) intersects an ambient neighborhood contained in T_i. Rescaling each shortened interval and taking the finite disjoint union gives a bijective collar Y×[0,1]→the union of those strips. Continuity follows from the finite clopen decomposition of Y, and its inverse follows either piecewise from the disjoint U_i or from compactness of the domain and Hausdorffness of X. This proves both directions under the stated separation and indexing hypotheses. The source’s “une partie finie” is retained; it can mean a finite collection here and is not changed to H’s proposed famille.

Counterexample to the weaker quasi-compact variant of N05, without a Hausdorff convention or an additional requirement that each collar neighborhood be closed in X. Form X from two copies of [0,1] by identifying equal t>0 and keeping their origins o_1,o_2 distinct. It is quasi-compact as a quotient of a finite disjoint union of compact intervals. Each {o_i} is closed. The subset U_i={o_i} union (0,1] is open in X and is homeomorphic to [0,1], so it is a product collar of its origin. The pair Y={o_1,o_2} is closed and discrete as a subspace. It has no collar: if Y×[0,1] embedded as a neighborhood T with the prescribed zero section, its two clopen product components, intersected with an ambient open neighborhood of Y contained in T, would give disjoint ambient open neighborhoods of the two origins. Every neighborhood of either origin contains a positive initial interval, so any two such neighborhoods intersect. This is a contradiction. The example refutes only that weakened interpretation of compact; it does not refute the manuscript statement under the customary compact-Hausdorff convention. If another page imposes closed collar neighborhoods or a separated-space convention, this particular example does not satisfy those strengthened hypotheses. No other page was consulted.

Targeted typing diagnostic for the diagonal marginal map. The upper target is literally [0,1], while the lower rule is y↦(y,0). For a general topological space Y, the pair (y,0) is an element of Y×[0,1], not of [0,1]. Thus the written two-row map has a type mismatch unless an unstated special identification is imposed. The natural repaired target would be Y×[0,1], consistent with the preceding product isomorphism, but that repair is not put into the transcription. The upper connector itself has no secure head, so its direction is also left doubtful.

The final lower index is J-shaped and is retained as J|I doubt beside the earlier clear I. If it is literally J and differs from I, the collection being unioned is not specified by the preceding clause, so N05 is a proof only for the intended same-index formulation, not a validation of an undefined J. Ink alone does not decide whether this is an authorial slip, a compressed I, or an unprovided convention. The operator bar(E)p_epsilon(T) has a true additional overbar above E only, a separate p and baseline (T); its interpretation is not used to remove the source’s separate first epsilon/delta/lambda ambiguity.

Revision and punctuation diagnostics. The isolated raised É/E is not expanded to Évitons, and the slanted word structure is transcribed only in the margin where it is written. The two Y variables visibly overwrite earlier Z forms; both layers are preserved. The heavy initial cylindrique group does not yield an independently readable additional cancelled word. Both main homéom forms have no stop, but the marginal homéom. has a real dot. The source writes cônique twice. Root audit identifies the isolated irregular blot below faux as lacking a recoverable linguistic or geometric structure; the draft graphic is removed and its crop remains available. The final le sont, with sont now explicitly uncertain, reaches the paper edge without a recoverable following full stop. A curved insertion leader at (absolu) and one at en général are attachment strokes, not extra parentheses/underlines. These are source-state decisions, not mathematical emendations.

Independent root audit personally inspected all 16 nonidentical crops, including the isolated blot and the complete triangle/marginal map, and a wider native-image opening. Five boxes were revised. First/second readings and their hashes remain fixed; final adjudications record the exclusion of the nonsemantic blot separately from actual source changes.

check_events.outcome: Verified the X=T boundary counterexample mechanism; did not reconstruct unavailable formula (7).
Constructed mutually inverse continuous maps for the mapping cylinder of a homeomorphism and the product collar; converse by transport of structure, under the stated interpretation of cônique.
Constructed endpoint collar coordinates and disjoint endpoint substrips; checked only positive radii/nondegenerate strips and explicitly conditional interpretation of the undefined strip operator.
Proved the finite disjoint closed-union collar equivalence in compact Hausdorff X with a common finite index set; used normality and compactness/tube shrinking explicitly.

Refuted N05.Q, the weakened quasi-compact/non-Hausdorff version with collars merely neighborhoods, by the compact interval with two origins. This does not refute N05.H, the compact-Hausdorff same-index version proved in N05, nor a separately imposed closed-collar formulation.
Checked the types: y↦(y,0) naturally lands in Y×[0,1], while the manuscript target is [0,1]. Retained the written target and the connector uncertainty.
Separated the literal unresolved J/I index from the same-index hypothesis needed for the finite-union proof; no formula was silently regularized.

notes.text: The sheet is manuscript text in his hand, with author number 2), a diagonal left-margin note, two mathematical diagram blocks, numerous revisions, and thin lower-left foliation 13 in another or undetermined hand. The entire original and both supplied native halves were read once; all fifteen saved crops were inspected once. P10 is rotated 45 degrees clockwise for reading, while every recorded coordinate remains in the original 1685 by 2363 image. The main text has nineteen physical prose lines, one equality display and one triangular diagram block (line_count 21 by this convention); the diagonal margin is inventoried separately. H’s foliation discussion, note about its added vertical arrow and proposed famille correction are editorial, not manuscript text.

Targeted boundary check. The source says “Mais on ne peut pas dire … en général que dot T soit la frontière de T dans X” and gives X=T with dot T not equal to the written 0. For any space X, the topological boundary of X inside itself is closure_X(X) minus interior_X(X), hence empty. Taking a nonempty Y and X=T=Y×[0,1], with the distinguished outer section dot T=Y×{1}, gives a nonempty dot T and empty ambient frontier. Thus the displayed counterexample mechanism is valid. This checks that mechanism only: reference (7) is read from its ink and the unavailable earlier statement numbered (7) is not reconstructed. The source’s un-crossed oval 0 is retained, not silently changed to phi or an empty-set glyph.

Independent local re-proof of the collar/mapping-cylinder equivalence, conditional on cônique having its usual mapping-cylinder meaning here. Let f:B→Y be a homeomorphism and let C(f) be the quotient of Y disjoint union (B×[0,1]) by (b,0) identified with f(b). The map sending the base y to (y,0) and the class of (b,r) to (f(b),r) is well-defined and continuous by the quotient property. Its inverse sends (y,r) to the class of (f^{-1}(y),r); this is continuous and agrees with the base identification at r=0. The two maps compose to the identities, so C(f)≃Y×[0,1] and the base inclusion becomes y↦(y,0), precisely the commutativity of diagram (10). Conversely a product collar transports the identity-map cone structure on Y×[0,1]. This proof uses an explicitly stated interpretation of the cone construction; the assigned leaf does not define all of its earlier notation. No extra bar on T is justified by this interpretation.

Targeted check of the absolute-cone and strip examples. Under the standard radial convention, away from the cone vertex the absolute cone on B has the product coordinates B×(0,1]. For any 0<a<1, the strip B×[a,1] is a collar neighborhood of the outer section B×{1}; the coordinate u=(1-r)/(1-a) sends that section to u=0 and gives B×[0,1]. For a positive radius lambda, the same construction on [a lambda,lambda] collars the section B×{lambda} inside the truncated cone T_lambda. This requires lambda>0; the source’s line does not state its range anew, and no assertion about the vertex radius zero is inferred. For a product strip B×[a,b] with a<b, each endpoint section has a collar obtained by a sufficiently short endpoint subinterval. Their union has a collar by choosing two disjoint endpoint subintervals and taking the disjoint union of those product collars. Therefore the three listed boundary choices are valid if the live barred-E-p operator denotes that radial strip and 0<epsilon<1. The operator is not defined on this leaf, so that identification and parameter range remain explicit hypotheses, not purported recovered definitions. The first epsilon/delta/lambda reading remains unresolved despite the expected strip formula.

Refined statement `150_scan014.N05.H`: Independent re-proof of the closing finite-union statement under the compact-Hausdorff convention, and assuming the uncertain lower J/I denotes the same finite index set as the preceding family. Let Y_i be finitely many pairwise disjoint closed subsets of compact Hausdorff X, and write Y for their union. Each Y_i is clopen in Y. If h:Y×[0,1]→T is a collar with h(y,0)=y and T a neighborhood of Y, then h(Y_i×[0,1]) is a neighborhood of Y_i: its product component is open in T, and intersecting it with an ambient open neighborhood of Y contained in T gives an ambient open neighborhood of Y_i. The restricted h is its collar. Conversely choose pairwise disjoint ambient open neighborhoods U_i of the Y_i, using normality for a finite family. For a collar h_i:Y_i×[0,1]→T_i, the preimage of U_i∩T_i is open and contains the compact zero section Y_i×{0}. A finite subcover by product neighborhoods provides delta_i>0 such that h_i(Y_i×[0,delta_i]) lies in U_i. Each shortened strip is still a neighborhood of Y_i: the smaller relatively open product Y_i×[0,delta_i) intersects an ambient neighborhood contained in T_i. Rescaling each shortened interval and taking the finite disjoint union gives a bijective collar Y×[0,1]→the union of those strips. Continuity follows from the finite clopen decomposition of Y, and its inverse follows either piecewise from the disjoint U_i or from compactness of the domain and Hausdorffness of X. This proves both directions under the stated separation and indexing hypotheses. The source’s “une partie finie” is retained; it can mean a finite collection here and is not changed to H’s proposed famille.

Counterexample to the weaker quasi-compact variant of N05, without a Hausdorff convention or an additional requirement that each collar neighborhood be closed in X. Form X from two copies of [0,1] by identifying equal t>0 and keeping their origins o_1,o_2 distinct. It is quasi-compact as a quotient of a finite disjoint union of compact intervals. Each {o_i} is closed. The subset U_i={o_i} union (0,1] is open in X and is homeomorphic to [0,1], so it is a product collar of its origin. The pair Y={o_1,o_2} is closed and discrete as a subspace. It has no collar: if Y×[0,1] embedded as a neighborhood T with the prescribed zero section, its two clopen product components, intersected with an ambient open neighborhood of Y contained in T, would give disjoint ambient open neighborhoods of the two origins. Every neighborhood of either origin contains a positive initial interval, so any two such neighborhoods intersect. This is a contradiction. The example refutes only that weakened interpretation of compact; it does not refute the manuscript statement under the customary compact-Hausdorff convention. If another page imposes closed collar neighborhoods or a separated-space convention, this particular example does not satisfy those strengthened hypotheses. No other page was consulted.

Targeted typing diagnostic for the diagonal marginal map. The upper target is literally [0,1], while the lower rule is y↦(y,0). For a general topological space Y, the pair (y,0) is an element of Y×[0,1], not of [0,1]. Thus the written two-row map has a type mismatch unless an unstated special identification is imposed. The natural repaired target would be Y×[0,1], consistent with the preceding product isomorphism, but that repair is not put into the transcription. The upper connector itself has no secure head, so its direction is also left doubtful.

The final lower index is J-shaped and is retained as J|I doubt beside the earlier clear I. If it is literally J and differs from I, the collection being unioned is not specified by the preceding clause, so N05 is a proof only for the intended same-index formulation, not a validation of an undefined J. Ink alone does not decide whether this is an authorial slip, a compressed I, or an unprovided convention. The operator bar(E)p_epsilon(T) has a true additional overbar above E only, a separate p and baseline (T); its interpretation is not used to remove the source’s separate first epsilon/delta/lambda ambiguity.

Revision and punctuation diagnostics. The isolated raised É/E is not expanded to Évitons, and the slanted word structure is transcribed only in the margin where it is written. The two Y variables visibly overwrite earlier Z forms; both layers are preserved. The heavy initial cylindrique group does not yield an independently readable additional cancelled word. Both main homéom forms have no stop, but the marginal homéom. has a real dot. The source writes cônique twice. A curved insertion leader at (absolu) and one at en général are attachment strokes, not extra parentheses/underlines. These are source-state decisions, not mathematical emendations.

notes.text: Undated handwritten page: formula (11) defines X*=X minus circled T=(X minus T) union dotted T and calls it a closed part of X. The proposition lists a), b), b-prime), and c) as equivalent conditions for a given 0<lambda<1; it then names a strict conic neighbourhood. A transverse note proposes germs of larger neighbourhoods. Two corollaries assert an ambient-frontier identity and strictness of scaled neighbourhoods. This is a transcription-only content account, not a proof of those statements.

Local source distinctions: every ordinary T has one cap and stem, without a further bar. Hollow-circle interior and filled-dot boundary symbols are distinct. Circumflexes are retained in cônique/côniques where visible; the author’s lui-= abbreviation is not expanded. Condition b has a clear final closing parenthesis but no separate live opening arc. Missing final stops after the strict definition and the last corollary are preserved. The additional triangular group in the second corollary is retained with token/state/caret uncertainty.

Conditional root counterexample to the opening closedness claim, using the literal cone-neighbourhood interpretation supplied by root (the first reader did not inspect another leaf): let X=([0,1]×{0}) union ({3/8}×[0,1]), Y={(0,0)}, T=[0,1/2]×{0}, dotted T={(1/2,0)}, with scalar action lambda·(t,0)=(lambda t,0). T is a closed neighbourhood of Y carrying the absolute cone structure. Its circled part is [0,1/2)×{0}. Therefore X*=X minus circled T omits the junction q=(3/8,0), but contains points (3/8,s) for s>0 tending to q. X* is not closed in X, although the displayed set identity (11) remains valid. The literal sentence “c’est une partie fermée de X” is unchanged.

Conditional root counterexample to the proposed equivalence in the same space, at the proposition parameter lambda=1/2: condition a holds under the collar interpretation supplied by root, since dotted T has the collar [1/2,1]×{0} inside X*. Condition c holds with T-prime=[0,1]×{0}; then T=lambda T-prime and the scalar structures agree. Condition b fails because every homeomorphism of X fixes its unique valence-three point q=(3/8,0), whereas q lies in T but not lambda T=[0,1/4]×{0}. Consequently b-prime, which adds requirements to b, also fails. These facts refute equivalence under the stated literal hypotheses; no corrected equivalence is claimed.

Qualification of the first frontier corollary in the same conditional example: the ambient frontier of T is {q,(1/2,0)}, whereas dotted T is only {(1/2,0)}. Thus if strictness is assigned by either a or c as proposed equivalent criteria, that corollary fails in this example. This does not assert failure under a definition that independently requires b. The obstruction is missing control of the ambient openness of circled T, not an error to be silently repaired in the transcription. No general sufficiency theorem for an added hypothesis is proved here.

The root supplied the example and its cone/collar interpretation; reader_a rechecked the coordinate membership, limiting vertical points, and valence obstruction in the course of recording it. Other-page definitions were not independently read. The second corollary and the marginal germ proposal are preserved without a separate general proof. The terminal marginal -R_{>0}-like group remains a reading doubt and receives no mathematical expansion.

Layout and hand attribution: the transverse note overlaps rectangular frames of main On dit and Corollaire text, which are not duplicated as marginal words. The small arrow-like stroke above the raised second-corollary T is the descender of the preceding frontière f, not an independent insertion arrow. The lower portion of the leaf is blank apart from thin foliation 14, whose hand attribution is indeterminate.

Independent audit: root inspected all 11 nonidentical second-reading crops and two enlarged target details. Four boxes gain narrowly stated uncertainty alternatives; their preferred readings are retained. No uncertainty-only addition has been promoted into a new primary C correction. The first/second readings remain fixed.

notes.text: Undated handwritten page: formula (11) defines X*=X minus circled T=(X minus T) union dotted T and calls it a closed part of X. The proposition lists a), b), b-prime), and c) as equivalent conditions for a given 0<lambda<1; it then names a strict conic neighbourhood. A transverse note proposes germs of larger neighbourhoods. Two corollaries assert an ambient-frontier identity and strictness of scaled neighbourhoods. This is a transcription-only content account, not a proof of those statements.

Local source distinctions: every ordinary T has one cap and stem, without a further bar. Hollow-circle interior and filled-dot boundary symbols are distinct. Circumflexes are retained in cônique/côniques where visible; the author’s lui-= abbreviation is not expanded. Condition b has a clear final closing parenthesis but no separate live opening arc. Missing final stops after the strict definition and the last corollary are preserved. The additional triangular group in the second corollary is retained with token/state/caret uncertainty.

Conditional root counterexample to the opening closedness claim, using the literal cone-neighbourhood interpretation supplied by root (the first reader did not inspect another leaf): let X=([0,1]×{0}) union ({3/8}×[0,1]), Y={(0,0)}, T=[0,1/2]×{0}, dotted T={(1/2,0)}, with scalar action lambda·(t,0)=(lambda t,0). T is a closed neighbourhood of Y carrying the absolute cone structure. Its circled part is [0,1/2)×{0}. Therefore X*=X minus circled T omits the junction q=(3/8,0), but contains points (3/8,s) for s>0 tending to q. X* is not closed in X, although the displayed set identity (11) remains valid. The literal sentence “c’est une partie fermée de X” is unchanged.

Conditional root counterexample to the proposed equivalence in the same space, at the proposition parameter lambda=1/2: condition a holds under the collar interpretation supplied by root, since dotted T has the collar [1/2,1]×{0} inside X*. Condition c holds with T-prime=[0,1]×{0}; then T=lambda T-prime and the scalar structures agree. Condition b fails because every homeomorphism of X fixes its unique valence-three point q=(3/8,0), whereas q lies in T but not lambda T=[0,1/4]×{0}. Consequently b-prime, which adds requirements to b, also fails. These facts refute equivalence under the stated literal hypotheses; no corrected equivalence is claimed.

Qualification of the first frontier corollary in the same conditional example: the ambient frontier of T is {q,(1/2,0)}, whereas dotted T is only {(1/2,0)}. Thus if strictness is assigned by either a or c as proposed equivalent criteria, that corollary fails in this example. This does not assert failure under a definition that independently requires b. The obstruction is missing control of the ambient openness of circled T, not an error to be silently repaired in the transcription. No general sufficiency theorem for an added hypothesis is proved here.

The root supplied the example and its cone/collar interpretation; reader_a rechecked the coordinate membership, limiting vertical points, and valence obstruction in the course of recording it. Other-page definitions were not independently read. The second corollary and the marginal germ proposal are preserved without a separate general proof. The terminal marginal -R_{>0}-like group remains a reading doubt and receives no mathematical expansion.

Layout and hand attribution: the transverse note overlaps rectangular frames of main On dit and Corollaire text, which are not duplicated as marginal words. The small arrow-like stroke above the raised second-corollary T is the descender of the preceding frontière f, not an independent insertion arrow. The lower portion of the leaf is blank apart from thin foliation 14, whose hand attribution is indeterminate.

Independent audit: root inspected all 11 nonidentical second-reading crops and two enlarged target details. Four boxes gain narrowly stated uncertainty alternatives; their preferred readings are retained. No uncertainty-only addition has been promoted into a new primary C correction. The first/second readings remain fixed.

notes.text: This manuscript leaf has author number read as 3) or 5) (3 preferred), a separate circled item 3, an opening replacement above a cancelled line, condition pair (12), a heavily revised NB, three lower marginal notes, a diagonal upper marginal definition, one unheaded marginal rule, and thin foliation 15. The full image and both supplied native halves were each inspected once, then all nineteen saved crops once. P09/P16/P17/P18 are rotated 45 degrees clockwise for readability; all boxes use original 1692×2365 coordinates. The main sequence occupies approximately twenty-five physical text/display rows, excluding raised and marginal additions. H’s page-order inference, explanatory comments, and supplied terminal ellipsis are editorial and are not source text.

The local mathematical content defines a conical subspace using (a) stability under interval homotheties and (b) a cone-neighborhood structure for the restricted operation. Its NB then asserts intrinsic-boundary and scaled-subspace intersection identities and describes such subspaces by a closed outer-boundary subset and a base subset containing its zero image. The upper margin calls the case with no extra base points strict. The final paragraphs define simultaneous compatibility with closed subspaces and a stronger compatibility involving an exterior cylindrical neighborhood. These descriptions are source summaries; the specific checks and failures are recorded separately below.

Independent radial-truncation counterexample to the two NB identities under the literal conditions (a),(b), using the interval-action mapping-cylinder definition supplied for this run. Take T=[0,1], Y={0}, with scalar action mu·t=mu t, and T-prime=[0,a] for 0<a<1. Condition (a) holds because 0≤mu t≤a for mu∈[0,1] and t∈[0,a]. The map h:[0,1]→[0,a], h(s)=as, is a homeomorphism fixing 0 and satisfies h(mu s)=mu h(s), so the restricted action on T-prime is again the absolute cone action. T-prime is also an ambient neighborhood of 0 in T because it contains [0,a), open relative to [0,1]. Thus the literal (b) is satisfied with the same Y={0}. But the intrinsic outer boundary of T-prime is {a}, whereas T-prime intersect dot T is [0,a] intersect {1}=empty. Also, for 0<lambda<1, lambda T-prime=[0,a lambda], whereas T-prime intersect T_lambda=[0,min(a,lambda)]. Taking a=lambda=1/2 gives [0,1/4] versus [0,1/2]. This refutes the implication from the printed local conditions alone to both NB identities. A stronger boundary-preserving, normalized-radius, or full-ambient-ray saturation convention could exclude this example, but such a condition is not present in (a),(b) as written. No source formula is repaired.

Targeted corrected-scope check of the reconstruction and strict correspondence. In a mapping cylinder C(f) of f:B→Y, write q for the quotient, with outer boundary B×{1}. For a closed subset A of B and a subspace C of Y satisfying f(A)⊂C, define S=q(A×[0,1]) union C. Then S has precisely A as its outer slice and C as its base intersection; it is invariant under the ambient scalar action. For every lambda∈[0,1], lambda S=C union q(A×[0,lambda]), and S intersect T_lambda is the same set. The source’s NB identities therefore hold for these full-ambient-ray saturated subcones. Conversely any such saturated S is uniquely determined by A=S intersect dot T and C=S intersect Y. Under the additional strict condition C=f(A), S is determined by A alone, proving the claimed closed-A/strict-subcone correspondence within this stronger class. The scalar-stable truncated example in N03 is not of this form. Closedness of A is retained as the source stipulates; it is not derived from conditions (a),(b) by this argument.

Independent topological check that the construction in N04 has the expected subspace topology when A is closed in B, without requiring C closed in Y. The natural continuous injection C(f restricted to A:A→C)→C(f) has image S. To prove it is an embedding, let F be closed in the smaller mapping cylinder. Its quotient preimages F_C⊂C and F_A⊂A×[0,1] are closed and compatible at zero. Extend F_C to a closed F_Y⊂Y with F_Y intersect C=F_C. Since A is closed in B, F_A is closed in B×[0,1]. The subset F_Y disjoint union (F_A union (f^{-1}(F_Y)×{0})) of Y disjoint union B×[0,1] is closed and saturated for the ambient quotient: zero-level membership agrees with F_Y, and compatibility of F_A at zero prevents an additional base identification. Its quotient image is closed in C(f), and its intersection with S is exactly F. Thus every closed set of the smaller cylinder is closed relative to S, which proves the embedding. This establishes the conditional construction used in N04, not the unrestricted classification asserted in the source NB.

Two separate base-variable diagnostics are preserved. First, condition (12)b ends in an unprimed Y, so read literally it makes T-prime a neighborhood of all of Y. The later classification permits a subspace Y-prime of Y containing only the zero image of the selected outer boundary. An arbitrary proper Y-prime need not contain all of Y. For example, for T=Y×[0,1] with two discrete base points and A one outer point, the strict saturated subcone A×[0,1] has only one base point and is not a neighborhood of the entire Y. Thus the classification with arbitrary Y-prime requires allowing a variable base, or retaining Y-prime=Y if (b) is literal. This is independent of the radial-truncation defect in N03. Second, the first lower variable in “et d’un sous-espace … de Y” is roofed T-prime-like, whereas the following inclusion clearly uses Y-prime. The transcript keeps T-prime|Y-prime doubt; the mathematical need for Y-prime does not decide the ink.

Compatibility diagnostic. With a fixed full-ray cone structure, compatibility with closed subspaces T_i or with X-prime is the requirement that the indicated intersections be conical for that same structure. The strict compatibility paragraph contains the literal words “avec T”, not “avec X-prime”; the surrounding preceding definition suggests X-prime may have been intended, but the written target is retained. Its exterior formulas are X-star=X minus ring T and X-prime-star=X-prime intersect X-star, with the raised sign on X-prime retained as star|r (star preferred), and with the hollow circle over T and primes preserved. The asserted alternative formulation stops after “et un iso”; the map and its compatibility requirements are not written on this leaf, so no completed equivalence is claimed or proved.

Punctuation, decoration and revision diagnostics. All ordinary T occurrences have one roof and stem, without an independent overbar. The interval parameter in (12)a is solid heavy I; the image formula has a two-stem I and a separate raised unreadable mark, retained by an empty-content doubt at its observed height. That mark is spatially separate from the preceding comma; its rendering asserts placement only, no named accent. The epsilon-like lowered group has uncertain cancellation state. In the image formula the following lambda/ell/brace-like group occupies normal letter height; its body and cancellation state remain uncertain. The apparent first compatible asterisk belongs to the hooked descender of fermée; only the later strictement compatible call has a separate star. The marginal rule is an independent unheaded stroke, not cancellation. Cônique/côniques is written with a separate accent in seven local occurrences, while other occurrences on this leaf remain unaccented. The terminal main-text iso has no supplied ellipsis; the live lower margin has exactly three points.

notes.text: This manuscript leaf has author number read as 3) or 5) (3 preferred), a separate circled item 3, an opening replacement above a cancelled line, condition pair (12), a heavily revised NB, three lower marginal notes, a diagonal upper marginal definition, one unheaded marginal rule, and thin foliation 15. The full image and both supplied native halves were each inspected once, then all nineteen saved crops once. P09/P16/P17/P18 are rotated 45 degrees clockwise for readability; all boxes use original 1692×2365 coordinates. The main sequence occupies approximately twenty-five physical text/display rows, excluding raised and marginal additions. H’s page-order inference, explanatory comments, and supplied terminal ellipsis are editorial and are not source text.

The local mathematical content defines a conical subspace using (a) stability under interval homotheties and (b) a cone-neighborhood structure for the restricted operation. Its NB then asserts intrinsic-boundary and scaled-subspace intersection identities and describes such subspaces by a closed outer-boundary subset and a base subset containing its zero image. The upper margin calls the case with no extra base points strict. The final paragraphs define simultaneous compatibility with closed subspaces and a stronger compatibility involving an exterior cylindrical neighborhood. These descriptions are source summaries; the specific checks and failures are recorded separately below.

Independent radial-truncation counterexample to the two NB identities under the literal conditions (a),(b), using the interval-action mapping-cylinder definition supplied for this run. Take T=[0,1], Y={0}, with scalar action mu·t=mu t, and T-prime=[0,a] for 0<a<1. Condition (a) holds because 0≤mu t≤a for mu∈[0,1] and t∈[0,a]. The map h:[0,1]→[0,a], h(s)=as, is a homeomorphism fixing 0 and satisfies h(mu s)=mu h(s), so the restricted action on T-prime is again the absolute cone action. T-prime is also an ambient neighborhood of 0 in T because it contains [0,a), open relative to [0,1]. Thus the literal (b) is satisfied with the same Y={0}. But the intrinsic outer boundary of T-prime is {a}, whereas T-prime intersect dot T is [0,a] intersect {1}=empty. Also, for 0<lambda<1, lambda T-prime=[0,a lambda], whereas T-prime intersect T_lambda=[0,min(a,lambda)]. Taking a=lambda=1/2 gives [0,1/4] versus [0,1/2]. This refutes the implication from the printed local conditions alone to both NB identities. A stronger boundary-preserving, normalized-radius, or full-ambient-ray saturation convention could exclude this example, but such a condition is not present in (a),(b) as written. No source formula is repaired.

Targeted corrected-scope check of the reconstruction and strict correspondence. In a mapping cylinder C(f) of f:B→Y, write q for the quotient, with outer boundary B×{1}. For a closed subset A of B and a subspace C of Y satisfying f(A)⊂C, define S=q(A×[0,1]) union C. Then S has precisely A as its outer slice and C as its base intersection; it is invariant under the ambient scalar action. For every lambda∈[0,1], lambda S=C union q(A×[0,lambda]), and S intersect T_lambda is the same set. The source’s NB identities therefore hold for these full-ambient-ray saturated subcones. Conversely any such saturated S is uniquely determined by A=S intersect dot T and C=S intersect Y. Under the additional strict condition C=f(A), S is determined by A alone, proving the claimed closed-A/strict-subcone correspondence within this stronger class. The scalar-stable truncated example in N03 is not of this form. Closedness of A is retained as the source stipulates; it is not derived from conditions (a),(b) by this argument.

Independent topological check that the construction in N04 has the expected subspace topology when A is closed in B, without requiring C closed in Y. The natural continuous injection C(f restricted to A:A→C)→C(f) has image S. To prove it is an embedding, let F be closed in the smaller mapping cylinder. Its quotient preimages F_C⊂C and F_A⊂A×[0,1] are closed and compatible at zero. Extend F_C to a closed F_Y⊂Y with F_Y intersect C=F_C. Since A is closed in B, F_A is closed in B×[0,1]. The subset F_Y disjoint union (F_A union (f^{-1}(F_Y)×{0})) of Y disjoint union B×[0,1] is closed and saturated for the ambient quotient: zero-level membership agrees with F_Y, and compatibility of F_A at zero prevents an additional base identification. Its quotient image is closed in C(f), and its intersection with S is exactly F. Thus every closed set of the smaller cylinder is closed relative to S, which proves the embedding. This establishes the conditional construction used in N04, not the unrestricted classification asserted in the source NB.

Two separate base-variable diagnostics are preserved. First, condition (12)b ends in an unprimed Y, so read literally it makes T-prime a neighborhood of all of Y. The later classification permits a subspace Y-prime of Y containing only the zero image of the selected outer boundary. An arbitrary proper Y-prime need not contain all of Y. For example, for T=Y×[0,1] with two discrete base points and A one outer point, the strict saturated subcone A×[0,1] has only one base point and is not a neighborhood of the entire Y. Thus the classification with arbitrary Y-prime requires allowing a variable base, or retaining Y-prime=Y if (b) is literal. This is independent of the radial-truncation defect in N03. Second, the first lower variable in “et d’un sous-espace … de Y” is roofed T-prime-like, whereas the following inclusion clearly uses Y-prime. The transcript keeps T-prime|Y-prime doubt; the mathematical need for Y-prime does not decide the ink.

Compatibility diagnostic. With a fixed full-ray cone structure, compatibility with closed subspaces T_i or with X-prime is the requirement that the indicated intersections be conical for that same structure. The strict compatibility paragraph contains the literal words “avec T”, not “avec X-prime”; the surrounding preceding definition suggests X-prime may have been intended, but the written target is retained. Its exterior formulas are X-star=X minus ring T and X-prime-star=X-prime intersect X-star, with the raised sign on X-prime retained as star|r (star preferred), and with the hollow circle over T and primes preserved. The asserted alternative formulation stops after “et un iso”; the map and its compatibility requirements are not written on this leaf, so no completed equivalence is claimed or proved.

Punctuation, decoration and revision diagnostics. All ordinary T occurrences have one roof and stem, without an independent overbar. The interval parameter in (12)a is solid heavy I; the image formula has a two-stem I and a separate raised unreadable mark, retained by an empty-content doubt at its observed height. That mark is spatially separate from the preceding comma; its rendering asserts placement only, no named accent. The epsilon-like lowered group has uncertain cancellation state. In the image formula the following lambda/ell/brace-like group occupies normal letter height; its body and cancellation state remain uncertain. The apparent first compatible asterisk belongs to the hooked descender of fermée; only the later strictement compatible call has a separate star. The marginal rule is an independent unheaded stroke, not cancellation. Cônique/côniques is written with a separate accent in seven local occurrences, while other occurrences on this leaf remain unaccented. The terminal main-text iso has no supplied ellipsis; the live lower margin has exactly three points.

The opening verb preference and the full-height placement of the looped formula group change; new alternative-only doubts elsewhere do not create new primary C corrections. All first/second readings remain fixed.

notes.text: This undated handwritten leaf bears a heavy upper 4), a lower circled 4 with a separate point, and thin lower-left foliation 17. The body defines compatibility of a partie-bord with a family through a cylindrical neighbourhood, then strict compatibility of a conic neighbourhood using the complementary X* and its induced family. It begins definitions of equisingularity via locally trivial fibrations. These are source-content descriptions, not proof claims. The final sentence stops after the locally doubtful même and is not completed.

Insertion and cancellation scope were read separately from word identity. B de X has one curved attachment and is followed by one live est; H’s extra struck est is not independently on the page. The au sens cylindrique insertion attaches after compatible, and its doubtful closing arc meets the main-line y. strict has two underlines; strictement has one underline plus a distinct attachment leader, fully captured in completing crop P17. The long elle ... et si insertion includes its final et si. The main line physically divides seule-/ment. The upper marginal note has no secure terminal stop; no quote marks were supplied.

The inserted formula is preserved literally as X_i\cap T=\mathbf I.X_i\cap\dot T-, including its heavy serif interval symbol, multiplication point, lack of supplied grouping parentheses, and final dash. No operand, union term or missing sign is completed. Main T forms have one roof, not an added bar. This paragraph is a transcription/formula-scope observation, not a verification of the displayed condition.

The lower definition literally says les Y_i sont coniques after introducing a family T_i\subset T. The forked Y has no T roof; H’s T_i is not adopted. The first équisingulier has an independent acute, whereas the second equisingulier has none identifiable. First relation: dotted T, a short upper dash, a longer lower unheaded/bent shaft, and Y; its role remains doubtful. The later dotted-T_i-to-Y relation has a definite two-sided arrowhead. The two relations are not silently made identical.

The large transverse margin is not a container for overlapping upright body text. P10 was made from original [16,855,480,1585], rotated clockwise45 (expanded846×846), then scaled to2600×2600. Inverse mapping sends the large cross/return after the final marginal Y to approximately original x273–402,y1296–1309, centred at (325,1309): the main-line X_i already transcribed in P08. The lower long downward stroke maps from about (293,1431) to (406,1421): the main-line ment continuation. A rotated cross near the earlier cancelled equality maps to (338,1015), also upright-body X-star ink. These are excluded from the margin. In contrast, the short dash before its live zero-image equality maps to (51,1472) and is genuinely marginal. The final marginal formula has an overbar above its right side, not a source underline.

Targeted conditional check of the marginal i.e.: interpret dot X_i as X_i\cap dot T, the zero action as the retraction to Y, and the final overbar as closure in X of X_i\setminus(X_i\cap Y). For a closed conic-compatible X_i, equality 0.dot X_i=X_i\cap Y implies the density formula: for each y in the intersection choose a boundary point b with 0.b=y; the positive points t.b approach y as t tends to zero and remain outside Y. Points already outside Y need no approximation. Closedness then gives X_i=cl_X(X_i\setminus Y). Conversely, density gives only density of the zero-image in X_i\cap Y under the conic-ray interpretation: a continuous zero retraction sends approximating positive rays to 0.dot X_i. Continuity does not make that image closed or surjective. This is a limited proof check of the two conditions, not a proof of all source definitions.

The converse in the marginal i.e. is refuted by the following explicit example, proposed by root and independently checked here. Put A=(0,1], Y=[0,1], f:A\to Y the inclusion, and let X be the quotient of Y disjoint-union (A×[0,2]) identifying (a,0) with f(a). Let T be Y together with the images of A×[0,1], dot T=A×{1}, use the usual scalar action on heights in T, and take X_i=X (closed). Y and T are closed; T contains the open neighbourhood consisting of Y and heights<1. Its exterior X* is A×[1,2], so dot T has the explicit product collar there. Compatibility with X_i=X is automatic. If a stronger strictness formulation requires shrinking by a homeomorphism, the increasing piecewise-linear height map h_lambda(t)=lambda*t on [0,1] and h_lambda(t)=lambda+(2-lambda)*(t-1) on [1,2] fixes0,2 and sends1 to lambda; it descends to the quotient fixing Y and sends T to lambda T. The positive part X\setminus Y is dense: every neighbourhood of y in Y has an open Y portion meeting A; if a is in that intersection, openness in the cylinder gives points (a,t) with t>0 in the neighbourhood. Thus X_i=cl_X(X_i\setminus Y)=X. However 0.dot X_i=f(A)=(0,1] is a proper subset of X_i\cap Y=[0,1]. Therefore the displayed density condition does not in general imply the zero-image equality, even with the explicit strict ambient collar. No source formula has been corrected.

The counterexample in N07 addresses the marginal i.e. between zero-image equality and density. The main inserted expression has the literal unfinished-looking ending X_i\cap T=I.X_i\cap dot T-. If that separate expression is completed/interpreted as the exact stronger hypothesis X_i\cap T=I·(X_i\cap dot T), then, under the usual conic-ray interpretation, intersecting with Y already imposes X_i\cap Y=0.dot X_i. N07 does not satisfy that extra equality, and is not claimed to refute a definition that includes it. The unclear terminal dash and the missing grouping are preserved rather than resolved by this diagnostic.

notes.text: This undated handwritten leaf bears a heavy upper 4), a lower circled 4 with a separate point, and thin lower-left foliation 17. The body defines compatibility of a partie-bord with a family through a cylindrical neighbourhood, then strict compatibility of a conic neighbourhood using the complementary X* and its induced family. It begins definitions of equisingularity via locally trivial fibrations. These are source-content descriptions, not proof claims. The final sentence stops after the locally doubtful même and is not completed.

Insertion and cancellation scope were read separately from word identity. B de X has one curved attachment and is followed by one live est; H’s extra struck est is not independently on the page. The au sens cylindrique insertion attaches after compatible, and its doubtful closing arc meets the main-line y. strict has two underlines; strictement has one underline plus a distinct attachment leader, fully captured in completing crop P17. The long elle ... et si insertion includes its final et si. The main line physically divides seule-/ment. The upper marginal note has no secure terminal stop; no quote marks were supplied.

The inserted formula is preserved literally as X_i\cap T=\mathbf I.X_i\cap\dot T-, including its heavy serif interval symbol, multiplication point, lack of supplied grouping parentheses, and final dash. No operand, union term or missing sign is completed. Main T forms have one roof, not an added bar. This paragraph is a transcription/formula-scope observation, not a verification of the displayed condition.

The lower definition literally says les Y_i sont coniques after introducing a family T_i\subset T. The forked Y has no T roof; H’s T_i is not adopted. The first équisingulier has an independent acute, whereas the second equisingulier has none identifiable. First relation: dotted T, a short upper dash, a longer lower unheaded/bent shaft, and Y; its role remains doubtful. The later dotted-T_i-to-Y relation has a definite two-sided arrowhead. The two relations are not silently made identical.

The large transverse margin is not a container for overlapping upright body text. P10 was made from original [16,855,480,1585], rotated clockwise45 (expanded846×846), then scaled to2600×2600. Inverse mapping sends the large cross/return after the final marginal Y to approximately original x273–402,y1296–1309, centred at (325,1309): the main-line X_i already transcribed in P08. The lower long downward stroke maps from about (293,1431) to (406,1421): the main-line ment continuation. A rotated cross near the earlier cancelled equality maps to (338,1015), also upright-body X-star ink. These are excluded from the margin. In contrast, the short dash before its live zero-image equality maps to (51,1472) and is genuinely marginal. The final marginal formula has an overbar above its right side, not a source underline.

Targeted conditional check of the marginal i.e.: interpret dot X_i as X_i\cap dot T, the zero action as the retraction to Y, and the final overbar as closure in X of X_i\setminus(X_i\cap Y). For a closed conic-compatible X_i, equality 0.dot X_i=X_i\cap Y implies the density formula: for each y in the intersection choose a boundary point b with 0.b=y; the positive points t.b approach y as t tends to zero and remain outside Y. Points already outside Y need no approximation. Closedness then gives X_i=cl_X(X_i\setminus Y). Conversely, density gives only density of the zero-image in X_i\cap Y under the conic-ray interpretation: a continuous zero retraction sends approximating positive rays to 0.dot X_i. Continuity does not make that image closed or surjective. This is a limited proof check of the two conditions, not a proof of all source definitions.

The converse in the marginal i.e. is refuted by the following explicit example, proposed by root and independently checked here. Put A=(0,1], Y=[0,1], f:A\to Y the inclusion, and let X be the quotient of Y disjoint-union (A×[0,2]) identifying (a,0) with f(a). Let T be Y together with the images of A×[0,1], dot T=A×{1}, use the usual scalar action on heights in T, and take X_i=X (closed). Y and T are closed; T contains the open neighbourhood consisting of Y and heights<1. Its exterior X* is A×[1,2], so dot T has the explicit product collar there. Compatibility with X_i=X is automatic. If a stronger strictness formulation requires shrinking by a homeomorphism, the increasing piecewise-linear height map h_lambda(t)=lambda*t on [0,1] and h_lambda(t)=lambda+(2-lambda)*(t-1) on [1,2] fixes0,2 and sends1 to lambda; it descends to the quotient fixing Y and sends T to lambda T. The positive part X\setminus Y is dense: every neighbourhood of y in Y has an open Y portion meeting A; if a is in that intersection, openness in the cylinder gives points (a,t) with t>0 in the neighbourhood. Thus X_i=cl_X(X_i\setminus Y)=X. However 0.dot X_i=f(A)=(0,1] is a proper subset of X_i\cap Y=[0,1]. Therefore the displayed density condition does not in general imply the zero-image equality, even with the explicit strict ambient collar. No source formula has been corrected.

The counterexample in N07 addresses the marginal i.e. between zero-image equality and density. The main inserted expression has the literal unfinished-looking ending X_i\cap T=I.X_i\cap dot T-. If that separate expression is completed/interpreted as the exact stronger hypothesis X_i\cap T=I·(X_i\cap dot T), then, under the usual conic-ray interpretation, intersecting with Y already imposes X_i\cap Y=0.dot X_i. N07 does not satisfy that extra equality, and is not claimed to refute a definition that includes it. The unclear terminal dash and the missing grouping are preserved rather than resolved by this diagnostic.

Independent audit: root personally inspected all 24 nonidentical boxes, the full slanted-margin crops and a wider native-orientation context. Six boxes were revised. The raised et underline is restored; the cancelled equality now prefers plain right-hand X_i; the lower adjective now prefers live strict with its earlier deletion reading retained as an alternative. Other new alternatives retain the earlier preferred text and do not create primary C corrections. Fixed first/second readings remain unchanged.

The density⇒zero-image-equality converse of the marginal i.e. fails in the height-[0,2] mapping-cylinder example. Checked density, proper zero image, closed X_i, ambient collar and the descended piecewise-linear shrinking homeomorphism. Scope is refined by N08; no claim is made against an additional exact orbit-generation hypothesis.
